body:
1.  OUR ATTENTION HAS BEEN DRAWN TO THE CASE OF PHAM NGOC
THU, FORMERLY THE US AMBASSADOR'S DRIVER DURING TENURES OF
AMBASSADORS UNGER AND SULLIVAN.  ACCORDING TO OUR INFORMA-

OF DIFFICULTIES PRESENTLY ENCOUNTERED BY CERTAIN FOREIGNERS,
INCLUDING VIETNAMESE, IN LEAVING LAOS.
4.  WE WOULD APPRECIATE A REPORT ON THIS CASE, WHAT CAN BE
DONE AND IF YOU REQUIRE FURTHER INSTRUCTIONS.  INGERSOLL

400. Increased criticism being aimed Chen Cheng method handling military situation since arriving Mukden. While praising Chen personally for his honesty and good intentions, question his judgment and leadership. Chen has no effective contact with subordinates, consequently does not have their confidence and does not have an integrated military machine so imperative present time. Chen even being blamed for his corruption suppression activities under which corrupt but capable military men were displaced without being effectively replaced. Some contend Chen should have wielded efficient military machine and then, when Communist situation dealt with, started his anti-corruption campaign. Chen planned win westerners' confidence by his anti-corruption program but was either incapable or unwilling to go full extent with corrective measures and thus win people's confidence. He now enjoys confidence of neither people nor his official associates.

title: PRG REPRESENTATION OSLO
body:
1.  NORWEGIAN DCM SVERRE CALLED ON EA DEPUTY ASSISTANT
SECRETARY MILLER FEBRUARY 18 TO DISCUSS LATEST POLITICAL
AND MILITARY SITUATION IN INDOCHINA.  AT END OF GENERAL
REVIEW, MILLER, CITING REPORT REFTEL A, RAISED ISSUE OF
POSSIBLE UPGRADING OF PRG REPRESENTATION IN OSLO.  MILLER
STRONGLY URGED GON NOT TO TAKE SUCH ACTION, POINTING OUT
PRG'S LACK OF GOVERNMENTAL STATUS AND EMPHASIZING THAT ANY
MOVE TO ENHANCE STATUS OF PRG AT TIME WHEN HANOI HAD
SHARPLY STEPPED UP ITS MILITARY OPERATIONS IN SOUTH WOULD
BE MOST UNFORTUNATE.  SVERRE REPLIED THAT HE HAD NO INDICA-
TION GON WAS CONSIDERING UPGRADING PRG REPRESENTATION
AT PRESENT TIME BUT THAT HE WOULD COMMUNICATE USG'S CONCERN
ON THIS ISSUE TO HIS GOVERNMENT.
2. MILLER ALSO TOOK OPPORTUNITY TO EXPRESS TO SVERRE U.S.
APPRECIATION FOR NORWAY'S DECISION TO ABSTAIN DURING SERIES
OF KEY PROCEDURAL VOTES AT LAW OF WAR CONFERENCE IN GENEVA
EARLIER THIS MONTH. KISSINGER

title: GM RESPONSE ON KING\'S CADILLAC
body:
1.  GM DETROIT INFORMED DEPT THAT A TELEX FROM MS. JOANNA
OSWALD WAS SENT OCT 4 TO ASOKE MOTORS IN RESPONSE TO
INQUIRIES ABOUT PARTS FOR THE KING'S CADILLAC.  GM WAS
ABLE TO DETERMINE WHICH PARTS ARE NECESSARY BASED ON THE

PARTS ARE NEEDED, AND DESPITE THE AGE OF THE CAR WILL BE
ABLE TO SUPPLY PARTS TO COMPLETE THE 1971 ENGINE.

TO COMPLETE THE PROJECT.  GOOD LUCK.   VANCE

title: STUDENT UNREST AT ALEXANDRIA UNIVERSITY
body:
1. CONGEN HAS BELATEDLY LEARNED THAT STUDENTS OF ENGINEERING
FACULTY OF ALEXANDRIA UNIVERSITY ATTEMPTED DEMONSTRATE AND
HAD CLASH WITH SECURITY FORCES ON JANUARY 3.
2. ACCORDING WELL-INFORMED SOURCE, ENGINEERING SCHOOL HAS
LONG BEEN KNOWN AS STRONGEST PRO-COMMUNIST STUDENT GROUP.
PRESUMABLY IN CONNECTION WITH RECENTLY REPORTED ARRESTS OF
ALLEGED COMMUNISTS GOE CLAIMS HAVE BEEN STIRRING UP TROUBLE
(REFTEL), STUDENT ACTIVIST LEADER NAMED MARWANI (OR MELWANI)
WAS ARRESTED ON JANUARY 2. FOLLOWING DAY HIS SISTER
CAME TO ENGINEERING SCHOOL AND SOUGHT STUDENT SUPPORT
FOR HIS RELEASE. STUDENTS RALLIED TO HER AND DECIDED
TO MARCH THROUGH CITY TO UNIVERSITY'S ARTS AND SCIENCES
CAMPUS MILE OR TWO DISTANT TO URGE STUDENT SUPPORT THERE.
3. POLICE INTERVENED TO PREVENT MARCH AND SOME SPIRITED
SCUFFLING BROKE OUT. FOURTEEN STUDENTS WERE ARRESTED.
FOLLOWING MOSLEM SABBATH JANUARY 4 STUDENTS QUIETED DOWN,
BUT ENGINEERING SCHOOL STILL UNDER CLOSE SURVEILLANCE OF
INTERNAL SECURITY PERSONNEL.
CHASE
EILTS

title: No. 336.Mr. Schuyler to Mr. Fish.
body:
No. 68.]

Sir: I have the honor to inform you that Governor Orr arrived here on the evening of March 15. Yesterday, by appointment, I called with him on Prince Gortchacow, who received us very cordially, and informed Governor Orr that he had already spoken to the Emperor, who would receive him the next day. As the interval between arrival and audience is often a week or ten days, this dispatch was, I think, intended as a special compliment to the representative of the United States.
Governor Orr accordingly had an audience from the Emperor to-day, and, with the delivery to him of the archives of the legation, my duties as charge d'affaires cease. I trust I have been able to perform them to the satisfaction of the Government.
I have, &c.,

EUGENE SCHUYLER.

title: The Secretary of State to the Consul General at Beirut (Palmer)
body:
The Secretary of State refers to the Consulate General's despatch no. 504, of March 20, 1940, regarding the transfer of inheritances from the mandated territory to heirs domiciled in the United States, and encloses herewith, for the Consulate General's information, a copy of an instruction on the subject which has been sent to the American Embassy in Paris.

The Consulate General is requested to report to the Department any further information it may obtain concerning this subject, with particular regard to the question of discrimination against heirs domiciled in the United States as compared with heirs domiciled in France or Great Britain.
Copies of any despatches sent to the Department on the subject should be forwarded direct to the Embassy in Paris.

title: Mr. Woodford to Mr. Sherman.
body:
No. 161.]
Sir: I have the honor to report that yesterday I telegraphed you in cipher as follows: 
Madrid, February 27, 1898.
Decree dissolving the Spanish Cortes was signed February 26. New Cortes will meet April 25.-- Woodford.

The practical effect of this delay in dissolving the old Cortes and assembling the new one on April 25 will be that the rainy season will have arrived in Cuba before the new Cortes gets fairly at work. With the beginning of the rainy season effective movements by the Spanish regular forces in Cuba will be impossible.
The Spanish Government will probably base argument on the then condition of military movements as reason for further delay.
Very respectfully, yours,


Stewart L. Woodford.

title: No. 423Editorial Note
body: On October 7, Prime Minister Churchill wrote to President Eisenhower proposing a bilateral meeting at the Azores in the following week. The President replied 3 days later that his schedule made this impossible, but suggested a meeting of their Foreign Ministers in Washington at that time. In a further exchange of messages it was decided that Secretary Dulles would go to London for a series of meetings with his British and French counterparts. For documentation on the preparations for and sessions at London, October 16-18, see volume VII, Part 1, pages 687 ff. During the course of the meetings in London, Secretary Dulles discussed the  ideas of a top-level four-power meeting and a solitary pilgrimage with Prime Minister Churchill.

2. DFA OFFICIAL SAID HIS DIVISION FRANKLY FAVORED THIS
EXCHANGE, PROVED ITS REPRESENTS FAIR GIVE AND TAKE, ADDING
THAT HIS OFFICE WOULD PROBABLY BE RESPONSIBLE FOR OVERSEEING
ANY PROJECT THAT MIGHT EVENTUATE. HE POINTED OUT THAT
SCIENTIFIC EXCHANGES WITH USSR HAVE BEEN SUSPENDED SINCE
LAST JUNE WHEN AUSTRALIANS FOUND LISTENING DEVICES IN THEIR
MOSCOW EMBASSY, AND ACCUSED THE SOVIETS OF SPYING ON
THEM. OFFICIAL SAID IT MAY BE SOME MONTHS BEFORE BAN
IS LIFTED. MOREOVER, HE OBSERVED, AUSTRALIAN SECURITY
SERVICE IS GENERALLY NEGATIVE CONCERNING EXCHANGES WITH
SOVIETS.

The German delegation takes note of the statement by the American delegation that while the Government of the United States makes no commitment binding upon its future conduct, it is not its present  practice or intention to transport to the United States any of the prisoners captured by its land forces who would be subject under the terms of this agreement to compulsory labor.

Stovall

title: Annual Meeting briefing papers, 1967 - Latin America - Briefing papers
body:
HONDURAS -9- September 18, 1967
The burden of Honduras! external public debt is not heavy.
The total external public debt at the close of 1966 amounted to
US$70 million, a little over half of it due to the World Bank.
Debt service payments in 1966 were US$3.5 million, equivalent to
2.4 percent of export earnings. If foreseeable additional loans,
of about US$85 million over the next four years, were all obtained
on conventional terms, debt service would rise to an estimated
5 percent of export earnings in 1970 and 6.5 percent in 1975.
This would be a substantial increase particularly in view of a
relatively tight budgetary position, and the Honduran Government
may therefore appropriately seek to borrow a portion of its needs
on concessional terms.
An economic mission is planned before the end of 1967 to
update these judgments.

20. British Minister during a conversation last night said if Congress repudiates agreement signed with him by Minister of Foreign Affairs his Government will avail itself of more forceful arguments. He intimated that absolute commercial boycott would be put into effect.
From other sources have learned that he has so threatened Costa Rican Government. England is principal market for Costa Rican coffee and boycott would be very harmful.
It is my opinion that Minister for Foreign Affairs and the President are anxious to accept British terms not only to avoid difficulties but also to diversify oil interests which with sole exception of  Amory holdings are American while Congress, because of feud with Executive Department in addition to its apparent disinclination to yield in the matter, may declare full support of law.

title: The Ambassador in Germany (Gerard) to the Secretary of State

[Telegram]

 
2277. Prominent German-American acquaintance of mine, head of large German concern, was called to Foreign Office and cross-examined for hour and half about possibility of German-American rising in arms against our Government. German defense union met May 20 in Prussian House of Deputies and adopted resolutions calling on the Chancellor to prevent by force export of arms from America. Gerard

title: 283. National Security Study Memorandum 25
body:
TO:
The Secretary of State
The Secretary of Defense
The Chairman, Atomic Energy Commission
The Director, Arms Control and Disarmament Agency
The Director of Central Intelligence
The President's Science Adviser
 The President has directed that a study be prepared on the relationship of the Cape Keraudren nuclear excavation project to the Limited Test Ban Treaty and the various options by which we might proceed with the project.
The study should be prepared by an ad hoc NSC group under the chairmanship of a representative of the Secretary of State, with representatives of the Secretary of Defense, Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission, Director of the Arms Control and Disarmament Agency, Director of Central Intelligence, Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and the President's Science Adviser.

Henry A. Kissinger

title: 238. National Security Study Memorandum 230
body:
TO
The Secretary of Defense
The Deputy Secretary of State
The Administrator, Agency for International Development
The Director of Central Intelligence
 The President has directed that a study be conducted regarding the establishment of a U.S. Sinai Support Mission pursuant to the U.S. Proposal of September 1, 1975, submitted in connection with the Agreement between Egypt and Israel of the same date. The study should analyze how best to organize and supervise the activities of a Sinai Support  Mission and should develop appropriate recommendations for effecting the provisions of the Proposal.
The study should be carried out by an ad hoc group comprised of representatives of the addressees and chaired by the representative of the Department of State. The study should be submitted to the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs not later than September 22, 1975, for consideration by the President.

Henry A. Kissinger

No. 258.]
Excellency: I have the honor to acknowledge the receipt of your note of the 28th ultimo, transmitting a copy of the Franco-German understanding reached at Paris on the 28th of September last, regarding a conference to be held at Algeciras for the purpose of considering measures looking toward an improvement of the present conditions in the Empire of the Shereef.
I note that the Sultan of Morocco has formally accepted the programme as well as the place of the conference.

The British Ambassador called at his request and I said that with respect to Djibouti and the confused situation existing there that to avoid bloodshed or danger of a clash among French factions with the serious risk of bad repercussions throughout northwest Africa at this critical time seriously affecting the military campaign there, this Government would suggest the advisability of the British and the American Governments each selecting an individual and these two persons in turn selecting a suitable Frenchman not conspicuously identified with either French faction and let him become the head of the French civil affairs at Djibouti. The Ambassador said that he would put that up to his Government.

C[ordell] H[ull]

Message dictated by Mr. Aldewereld from the London
Office at 4.00p.m., on llth June, 1968 to the
American Embassy, London for transmittal to
Mr. McNamara in Indonesia through the U.S. Ambassador,
Marshall Green in Jakarta.
 
Agreement reached with Lipfert on 400m DM private private placement
Grace period 8 years repayment 6 following years
Coupon 6)%
Their asking price 97-5/8 but this could be improved slightly.
Accelerated repayments after 8 years possible without penalty.
Lipfert will also guarantee that the paper will be absorbed in his
portfolio in event anyone wishes to sell.
Lipfert and associates will visit Washington from June 19 for final
discussions.
Both Blessing and Economic Ministry Bonn are in full agreement. They
consider price quite reasonable.
Guth also in agreement although reluctantly.
He igforms me that Deutsche Bank proposes public issue 200m DM either
August or September.
Returning Washington Wednesday.
Best Regards
Siem Aldewereld

body:
1.  CONFIDENTIAL - ENTIRE TEXT.
2.  ON NOVEMBER 26 DCM           DISCUSSED THE PRESENT
STATUS OF THE LANCASTER HOUSE NEGOTIATIONS WITH AMBASSADOR
OSOBASE, DIRECTOR OF MEA'S AFRICA DEPARTMENT, AND MADE
POINTS IN SUPPORT OF THE BRITISH SET FORTH IN REFTEL A.
DCM ALSO ADVANCED THE ARGUMENT THAT A COLLAPSE OF THE
NEGOTIATIONS WOULD DELIGHT THE SAG, WHICH IS PESSIMISTIC
REGARDING MUZOREWA'S CHANCES AGAINST THE PF IN AN ELECTION
(REFTEL B).  DCM SAID THAT NIGERIA'S INFLUENCE ON THE PF
HAD CONTRIBUTED MUCH TO THE ASTONISHING SUCCESS OF THE
LANCASTER HOUSE NEGOTIATIONS TO DATE AND SUGGESTED THAT
THE PROVISION OF ADDITIONAL ADVICE THIS WEEK COULD PERHAPS
PROVE DECISIVE.
3.  OSOBASE APPEARED SYMPATHETIC TO THESE REPRESENTATIONS

I showed this yesterday to the Secretary, who feels that the Russian Ambassador should communicate any comments he has to make to Paris through his colleague in Paris. He emphasizes the fact that these claims have been originated by Germany.




W. Phillips

 Have the Joint Staff and/or CINCLANT come up with an outline plan on what we could get into Cuba five days after the President says go, with an indication of what additional forces we could get if we had three more days. Mr. McNamara expressed his concern about the current account deficits
of the LDCs resulting from recent oil price increases. In his view, commercial
banks would probably not be able to bear the intermediation risk of channeling
OPEC surpluses to the LDCs to the same extent as they had done in the past.

risk was not carried to a large enough extent by the governments of OECD and OPEC.

the Bank's gearing ratio would enable the Bank to play such an enlarged role.

title: Memorandum by Mr. Carlton Savage, Assistant to the Assistant Secretary of State (Long)
body:
Mr. Gray informed me on December 13 that the Secretary had just been informed of the President's desire that there be no declaration  of war on any of the small European countries, such as Bulgaria, Hungary, and Rumania, who were reported in the press as having declared war against the United States. Mr. Gray said the Secretary desired that this information be given to any one at the Capitol who might be interested.
I gave the information to Senator Connally by telephone on the afternoon of December 13 and he said he agreed absolutely with the President. I could not reach Mr. Rayburn, Mr. McCormack, or Mr. Bloom on December 13, but I gave the information to Mr. Bloom's secretary on December 15 and to Mr. McCormack on December 16.


Carlton Savage

title: 141. Memorandum From Secretary of State Rogers to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Kissinger)
body:
I have reviewed the cables referred to in your memorandum of February 5.

The applicable part of the President's two directives to which you refer is that governing official communications, which states: "All official communications with policy implications must be cleared with the White House. When in doubt, the rule is that messages will be so cleared...."

Early in the Administration I established procedures within the Department concerning clearances with the White House. These procedures fully accord with the President's memoranda of September 1, 1969 and December 21, 1970. All of the cables mentioned in your memorandum were handled in accordance with these procedures. They do not in my view depart from policy established by the President, and I therefore do not consider that the question of policy implication arises.



William P. Rogers

title: ;: CZECHOSLOVAK HARVEST SITUATION
body:
1. CZECHOSLOVAK PRODUCTION TARGETED 10.8 MILLION TONS
OF GRAIN FOR 1978, OF WHICH 7 MILLION SHOULD BE HARVESTED
IN THE CZECH LAND AND 3.8 MILLION IN SLOVAKIA.  CZECH
HARVEST IS STILL THREE WEEKS AWAY, WHILE HARVEST IN
SLOVAKIA HAS COMMENCED.

CROP MATURING LATE -- ABOUT TWO WEEKS -- BECAUSE OF
CONTINUING BAD WEATHER.  MOREOVER, GRAIN APPEARS TO BE
RIPENING UNEVENLY.  REPORTS FROM THE CZECH LAND IN-
DICATE SAME PROBLEMS.
3. CZECHOSLOVAKIA WILL EXPERIENCE A DIFFICULT HARVEST
IF RAIN AND COLD WEATHER PREVAIL DURING THE COMING
WEEKS.  IN FACT, WEATHER COULD EVEN CAUSE SOME DOUBTS
THAT THE COUNTRY WILL MEET ITS PRODUCTION TARGET OF
10.8 MILLION TONS.
4. A MORE COMPREHENSIVE REPORT ON HARVEST SITUATION
WILL FOLLOW AFTER AGATTACHE VISITS WITH MIN. AG.
OFFICIALS EARLY IN AUGUST. WOLF

title: Editorial Note
body: The Department of State, on July 21, released a statement by Secretary of State Acheson on the Palestine problem. The key paragraph read as follows: "Now that the position of both parties have been fully defined in previous sessions of the [Palestine Conciliation] Commission,  it will materially advance the task of the Commission if both the Israeli and the Arab delegations return to Lausanne with full authority to enter into constructive and effective negotiations. It will also greatly facilitate the Commission's task if both sides will now extend their exchange of views to all problems covered by the General Assembly resolution of December 11, in order to make possible a simultaneous and balanced approach to the closely related problems of territoral settlement and disposition of the refugees from the hostilities." The full text of the Secretary's statement is published in Department of State Bulletin, August 1, 1949, page 148.

title: NETHERLANDS CENTRAL BANK INCREASES DISCOUNT RATE
body:
1. THE NETHERLANDS CENTRAL BANK ANNOUNCED, EFFECTIVE OCT 16, AN
INCREASE IN THE DISCOUNT RATE FROM 6.5 PERCENT TO 7 PERCENT. THIS
IS THE FIFTH INCREASE IN 1973.
2. THE BANK SAID IT RAISED ITS RATES TO BRING THEM INTO LINE
WITH MONEY MARKET RATES AND TO TAKE ACCOUNT OF THE CONTINUING
EXPANSION OF THE BANKS' CREDIT. THE BANK DECIDED TO CUT THE
EXTRA CHARGE ON BANKS WHICH MAKE EXCESSIVE CALLS ON THE CENTRAL
BANK TO TWO PERCENT FROM THREE PERCENT ON AN ANNUAL BASIS TO
REDUCE THE UPWARD PRESSURE ON THE MONEY MARKET RATES.
3. THE OTHER RATES OF THE CENTRAL BANK WERE ALSO INCREASED BY
1/2 PERCENT. THESE ARE NOW: PROMISSORY NOTE RATE: 8 PERCENT;
ADVANCES ON CURRENT ACCOUNT AND LOANS TO PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS:
9 PERCENT; ALL OTHER RATES: 8 PERCENT.
GOULD

title: LOCAL SITUATION, NAIROBI, KENYA
body:
1. NAIROBI HAS BECOME TENSE FOLLOWING ANNOUNCEMENT THAT A POPULAR
MEMBER OF THE KENYA PARLIAMENT WAS MURDERED. (DETAILS BEING RE-
PORTED SEPTEL).
2. A SMALL GROUP OF UNIVERSITY STUDENTS PASSED EMBASSY THIS MORNING
WITHOUT INCIDENT. LOCAL POLICE ADVISE THAT STUDENTS
ARE GATHERING AT THE UNIVERSITY, A MILE NORTH OF THE EMBASSY, AND
SMALL GROUPS OF PERSONS ARE GATHERING IN DOWNTOWN NAIROBI.
STUDENTS BEING CLOSELY OBSERVED BY LOCAL AUTHORITIES WHO SEEM TO
HAVE LOCAL SITUATION UNDER CONTROL. A LARGE NUMBER OF LOCAL
ESTABLISHMENTS HAVE CLOSED IN ANTICIPATION OF DISTURBANCES. THERE
IS NO INDICATION THE U.S. FACILITIES OR PERSONNEL ARE TARGETED.
3. DIRECT LIAISON HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED WITH LOCAL POLICE WHO ARE
ON FULL ALERT. KENYA ARMY AND AIR FORCE ALSO IN FULL ALERT.
RADIO COMMUNICATION HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED WITH ALL U.S.
FACILITIES; EMBASSY SECURITY INCREASED AND EACH U.S. AGENCY
BRIEFED ON PREVENTIVE ACTIONS.
4. WILL ADVISE FURTHER DEVELOPMENTS.
MARSHALL

title: POSSIBLE US SHIP VISIT
body:
REFERENCE: MOGADISCIO 1911
1. I ASKED FONSEC DEC. 30 ABOUT US NAVAL VISIT. HE WAS
QUITE VAGUE AND EVEN EXPRESSED UNCERTAINTY AS TO WHETHER WE
OR SOMALIS WERE SUPPOSED TO COME UP WITH SUGGESTED DATE. HE

WELL SEPARATED. WHEN I REMINDED HIM WE WERE WAITING FOR DATE
FROM GSDR HE ASKED CHIEF OF PROTOCOL TO CHECK WITH MINISTRY
OF DEFENSE.

PROPOSE IF FONSEC OR HIS COLLEAGUES THROW SELECTION OF DATE
BACK ON US. I WOULD THEREFORE APPRECIATE BEING GIVEN A COUPLE
OF ALTERNATIVE DATES WHICH I COULD SUGGEST TO GSDR IN SUCH AN
EVENT. IN VIEW OF WHAT FRENCH WERE TOLD (REFTEL), BEST TIME
MIGHT BE WITHIN LAST TEN DAYS OF JANUARY, WITH PERHAPS LATE
FEBRUARY AS ALTERNATE.

title: FORGED NIV REPORTED FOR FIRST TIME IN MEMORY, A FORGED U.S. VISA WAS  REPORTED TO THE
body:
FOR FIRST TIME IN MEMORY, A FORGED U.S. VISA WAS REPORTED TO THE
CONSULATE GENERAL. ALERT LOCAL PAN AMERICAN TICKET CLERK QUESTIONED
AUTHENTICITY OF B-1 VISA #001281 ALLEDGEDLY ISSUED 10 JUNE 1975
TO A MOHAMMED HABIB. HABIB THEN SNATCHED THE PASSPORT FROM CLERK'S
HANDS AND RAN FROM THE BUILDING. WE HAVE, THEREFORE, NOT SEEN
SUSPECTED FORGERY BUT CLERK REPORTS IT SIMILAR TO GENUINE
EXCEPT SOMEWHAT INDISTINCT AND SLIGHTLY SMUDGED. CLERK
BECAME SUSPICIOUS AS CONOFF'S SIGNATURE DID NOT LOOK GENUINE
(ALTHOUGH NAME WAS CORRECT) AND VISA WAS SIGNED IN BLUE INK.
POST RECORDS SHOW THAT VISA #001281 WAS B-2 ISSUED TO A GHULAM
AHMED ON 26 AUGUST 1974. HABIB HAS NOT BEEN FURTHER IDENTIFIED,
BUT POST HAS ELICITED CO-OPERATION OF LOCAL AUTHORITIES
IN ATTEMPT TO UNCOVER ADDITIONAL INFORMATION.
TIGER

HIGHER.  EMBASSY KUALA LUMPUR ALONE REPORTED 754
ARRIVALS IN MALAYSIA DURING SEPTEMBER, AND AN
ADDITIONAL 1271 DURING OCTOBER.

BANGKOK 25693 PROVIDED FIGURES OF 4775 FOR JULY 1977,
3716 FOR AUGUST AND 3661 FOR SEPTEMBER.  THE UNHCR

PER MONTH FOR THIS FOUR-MONTH PERIOD.

title: PRC HANDLING OF MAO'S DEATH IN MEXICO
body:
REF  : STATE 223128
1.  THE PRC EMBASSY'S HANDLING OF COMMEMORATIVE ACTIVITIES ON
MAO'S DEATH WAS LOW-KEYED. TURNOUT FOR SIGNING THE CON-
DOLENCE BOOK WAS VERY SPARSE. EMBASSY PERSONNEL, ON APPARENT
INSTRUCTIONS FROM PEKING, DID NOT PARTICIPATE IN ANY OUTSIDE
HOMAGES TO MAO.
2.  SURPRISINGLY CHINESE REPRESENTATIVES DECIDED TO ATTEND
THE VARIED INTERNATIONAL EVENTS IN MEXICO THAT IMMEDIATELY
FOLLOWED MAO'S DEATH. A PRC MILITARY DELEGATION TO THE
MEXICAN MILITARY AND INDEPENDENCE DAY EVENTS WAS ON ITS WAY
TO MEXICO WHEN THE DEATH WAS ANNOUNCED, BUT DID NOT TURN
BACK AS EVEN THE PRC EMBASSY HERE EXPECTED. THE DELEGATION
PARTICIPATED IN THE OFFICIAL FUNCTIONS, AND PRC EMBASSY
PERSONNEL ATTENDED THE INAUGURATION OF THE THIRD WORLD
INSTITUTE AND THE OPENING SESSIONS OF THE GROUP OF 77
CONFERENCE ON COOPERATION AMONG DEVELOPING NATIONS.
JOVA

title: 134. Telegram From the Chief of Naval Operations (Burke) to the Commander in Chief, Atlantic (Dennison)
body:
190217Z. Exclusive for Adm Dennison and RAdm Clark from Burke. Bumpy Road. I was asked once again if it were possible to land an experienced Marine (or Naval officer who has amphibious knowledge) on beach with CEF without danger of him being killed or captured or it becoming known U.S. was involved. The urgency stems from lack of knowledge here of true situation on beach and what should be done now without overtly involving United States. If Johnny thinks it could be done within his own resources with little danger it should be done. I have said it too likely to fail but I may be wrong.
Please advise, Exclusive to Burke only, on this one along with any further information on situation or comments on how to get dope.

title: President Wilson to the Secretary of State
body:
My Dear Mr. Secretary: I shall await the note from Chile with deep interest.
Will you not be kind enough to have a talk with Ambassador Naon and ascertain whether he got the impression from House that the Chilean Ambassador seems to have got, that we would not propose our treaty to the other countries of South and Central America unless all three of the A. B. C. approved. I remember nothing of the kind, and think Mr. Suarez must be mistaken.
I think it would be wise, as you suggest, to approach the Peruvian government very tactfully and ascertain whether they are willing to treat matters in dispute between them and Chile as the enclosed despatch suggests.

Faithfully Yours,

W. W.

IT ALSO GIVES PROMINENT PLAY TO REPORTED EGYPTIAN
MILITARY MOVEMENTS AND EGYPTIAN SECOND AND THIRD
ARMIES' HIGH STATE OF READINESS.

SPIRED PRESS STORIES HAVE A DUBIOUS CHARACTER TO THEM.
WELL ORCHESTRATED EFFORT IS CLEARLY UNDERWAY TO KEEP
LEVEL OF TENSION HIGH IN ORDER IMPRESS BOTH USG AND
ISRAEL NEED FOR URGENT MOVEMENT ON DISENGAGEMENT.
EILTS

The United Nations General Assembly met on December 14 from 10:45 a. m. to 1:50 p. m.; for the record, see U.N. document A/PV.324. At this meeting, the Assembly adopted as Resolution 384 (V) the text of the draft 13-power resolution which had been submitted to the First Committee on December 12, page 1524. The roll-call vote was 52 (including the United States) in favor, to 5 (Czechoslovakia, Poland, Byelorussian S.S.R., Ukrainian S.S.R., Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) opposed, with 1 (Republic of China) abstention.
At the 325th meeting of the General Assembly on the afternoon of December 14, the Assembly's President, Nasrollah Entezam of. Iran, announced that he along with Lester B. Pearson of Canada and Sir Benegal Rau of India would form the three-member committee to inquire into the basis on which a satisfactory cease-fire in Korea could be arranged (see U.N. document A/PV.325).

title: The Ambassador in Greece (MacVeagh) to the Secretary of State
body:
962. Varvaressos submitted resignation as Vice Prime Minister Sept 1 and despite efforts Regent and British colleague persuade him reconsider remains adamant. Has made no public statement explaining step but according British colleague is personally very bitter, charging he has been "ganged up on" chiefly by industrialists, later joined by Leftists in opportunist effort to exploit situation (see my telegram 941, Aug 30). Thinks his resignation will be "severe shock" resulting economic chaos and subsequent recall his services.
Govt undertaking to stabilize situation so as not to prevent Regent's going London. Has given statement to press that economic policy remains unchanged. Plans appoint new men supply and broaden Advisory Economic Committee perhaps with additional Leftist members, meanwhile trusting to assurances by industrialists that objections to Varvaressos not against policy but against method by which applied.
[
MacVeagh

title: Memorandum by the Minister in China (Johnson)
body:
In conversation with Dr. Frank Lee, Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs today, I referred to the question of Tientsin and the desire of the Chinese to stop and search vessels going in and out of Tientsin. Vice Minister Lee stated that he had heard nothing further in regard to the matter, that he had referred it to the Minister of Finance and also to the Ministry of the Navy. He mentioned the fact that in conversation with Admiral McVay the latter had objected to the idea of putting Customs officers on Chinese naval vessels and to the suggestion made that the naval vessels be turned over to the Customs for purposes of search. He stated that the Chinese Navy naturally objected to flying the Customs flag on naval vessels.
Nelson Trusler Johnson

WILLIAM H. SEWARD.

title: VIEWS AND DATA ON PROPOSED PANAMA CANAL TOLL INCREASE
body:
1. AFTER WAITING SEVERAL DAYS, EMBOFF WAS ABLE TO OBTAIN
APPOINTMENT MARCH 29 WITH FOREIGN MINISTRY OFFICIAL TO REQUEST
ECUADOREAN VIEWS ON PROPOSED 20 PERCENT TOLL INCREASE.
2. CRISTOBAL MONTERO, CHIEF OF ECONOMIC COOPERATION, IN
MINISTRY'S DIRECTORATE OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS, INFORMED EMBOFF
THAT ECUADOR SURELY WOULD BE AFFECTED BUT HAD NOT CALCULATED
FULL IMPACT ON ECUADOREAN ECONOMY. MONTERO NOTED THAT MOST
ECUADOREAN BANANA EXPORTS TO U.S. GO TO EAST COAST; THESE
WOULD BE AFFECTED AS WELL AS BANANAS DESTINED FOR EUROPEAN
MARKET. ECUADOREAN PETROLEUM BOUND FOR U.S. GULF PORTS AND
TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO REFINERIES WOULD ALSO BE AFFECTED.
3. MONTERO GAVE IMPRESSION THAT PROPOSED TOLL INCREASE
IS NOT UPPERMOST ON LIST OF MINISTRY'S CONCERNS. HOWEVER,
HE PROMISED TO FURTHER STUDY ISSUE AND PRESENT MINISTRY'S
VIEWS WITHIN NEXT SEVERAL DAYS. WE DOUBT, HOWEVER, THAT
THESE WILL BE RECEIVED BEFORE APRIL 1.
BREWSTER

PARTICIPANTS

title: The Chargé in the Philippines (Lockett) to the Secretary of State
body:
1805. Carlos Romulo today made to me statement summarized below:
He is seeking alter direction given Pacific Union by Chiang-Quirino conversations.... Romulo told Quirino he should first have approached Nehru, that Australia should be brought into planned union so it would not take on anti-white appearance and that elimination colonialism should be one of union's objectives. He also encountering difficulty persuading Quirino [that] Pacific Union should be publicized as non-Communist rather than anti-Communist and that it could later emerge as instrument through which member nations might cooperate combat Communism.
Romulo intends spend July and August working on plan for UN, but until he and President reach fundamental agreement he does not propose approach other governments. He hopes, however, evolve union nations this area which US will be able accept and this general connection made assertion State Department needs do some new thinking regarding Far East.


Lockett

title: PLO VISIT TO BANGKOK
body:
IN CONVERSATION WITH EGYPTIAN EMBASSY OFFICIAL ON AUG 10
EMBOFF WAS TOLD THAT PALESTINE LIBERATION ORGANIZATION (PLO
DELEGATION HAD BEEN PLEASED WITH THEIR RECENT TRIP TO SOUTH-
EAST ASIAN NATIONS.  THE EGYPTIAN OFFICIAL SAID PLO DID NOT
EXPECT MUCH FROM VISIT TO BANGKOK (SEE REFTEL) SINCE STOP
HERE HAD BEEN PRIMARILY TO ESTABLISH MEANS OF COMMUNICATION
WITH RTG AND PROVIDE OPPORTUNITY TO EXPLAIN PLO POSITION.
PLO, ACCORDING TO EGYPTIAN OFFICIAL, HAD NOT EXPECTED RTG
TO ALLOW ESTABLISHMENT OF A PLO OFFICE IN BANGKOK AND DE-
LIBERATELY HAD NOT PRESSURED RTG BECAUSE THEY RECOGNIZED
THAI SENSITIVITIES TO MIDDLE EAST SITUATION. DURING MEETING
WITH FOREIGN MINISTER UPPADIT, PLO REPORTEDLY DID MOST OF
THE TALKING--UPPADIT HAD BEEN "NICE" AND HAD LISTENED TO
PLO PRESENTATION BUT HAD NOT SAID MUCH IN REPLY, AC-
CORDING TO EGYPTIAN OFFICIAL.  EGYPTIAN OFFICIAL WAS
OPTIMISTIC THAT PLO WOULD SOON BE RECOGNIZED BY SEVERAL
ASIAN COUNTRIES.
O'DONOHUE

title: No. 435.Mr. Davis to Mr. Cayetano Romero.
body:
Sir: I have the pleasure to transmit to you, for the information of the Mexican Government, the inclosed copy of a letter from the War Department of the 13th instant, covering an unsigned telegram, but which is understood to have been sent by Brig. Gen. George Crook, United States Army, and from which it will appear that, in his recent and successful operations against the hostile Chiricahuas in Mexico, General Crook manifested a zealous observance of the spirit of the agreement between the United States and Mexico of July 29, 1882, which provides for the reciprocal crossing of the frontier by troops of either Government in pursuit of hostile Indians.
Accept, &c.,
JOHN DAVIS,Acting Secretary.

title: 227. Memorandum of Conversation
body:
PARTICIPANTS
Ambassador Simcha Dinitz
General Brent Scowcroft, Deputy Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs
Commander Jonathan T. Howe, NSC Staff

General Scowcroft began the meeting by reading the agreed text of a resolution which the U.S. and the Soviet Union had jointly agreed to submit to the Security Council that evening. General Scowcroft pointed out that the resolution:
--Leaves all Israeli forces in-place.
--Contains no reference to withdrawal, only a general reference to Resolution 242.
--Calls for direct negotiations between parties with joint U.S./Soviet auspices to facilitate.
--Includes a joint U.S./Soviet commitment to use maximum influence to bring about an exchange of prisoners.
General Scowcroft indicated that a call for a Security Council meeting would be initiated at 6:00 p.m. that evening. The only response made by the Ambassador was that the timetable was very tight.

title: Mr. Seward to Mr. Sullivan.
body:
No. 23.]

Sir: Your dispatch of the 16th of September, No. 25, has been received. It is accompanied by an interesting correspondence which you recently had with Mr. Hanaberg, United States consul at Carthagena, on a rumor that a citizen of the United States had been assassinated at Rio Hacha, and also concerning the case of the persons, lately citizens of the United States, who had enlisted in the Colombian service on board the Colombian steamer El Rayo. The reported assassination having proved to be without foundation, and the case of the persons enlisted on the steamer El Rayo having been already considered, I do not find it necessary to enlarge at the present time upon either of those matters.
I am, sir, your obedient servant,

WILLIAM H. SEWARD.
Peter J. Sulliyan, Esq., &c., &c., &c.

body:
[Telegram.]

 
752. The President is gratified to learn from your telegram No. 856, April 15, 9 p.m., that General Huerta is disposed to bring this unfortunate incident to a close by complying with Admiral Mayo's demand. He felt sure that this would be the result when the General understood the situation. If you will examine Mayo's demand you will see that it states that the salute will be returned. This I may add is the invariable custom, from which the Government would not of course depart. Now that Admiral Mayo's demand is to be acceded to, the sooner it is done the better and I suggest that General Huerta take the matter up at once through the proper channels.


Bryan.

ENTRY INTO COMMUNITY.

THE GOVERNMENT HAS ALLOCATED 218 MILLION GUILDERS (ONE DOLLAR NOW

MILLION AS A GRANT.

MILLION GUILDERS WILL BE USED TO IMPORVE THE INFRASTRUCTURE

title: JAPANESE/EC TARIFF PROGRESS
body:
1.  IN MCDONALD/UKAWA DISCUSSION ON WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON,
THE JAPANESE INDICATED FOR THE FIRST TIME THAT THEY ARE
MAKING SOLID PROGRESS WITH THE EC TOWARD A BALANCED TARIFF
SETTLEMENT.  UKAWA SAID THAT HE COULD NOW SEE PROSPECTS TO
WIND UP THEIR BILATERAL UNDERSTANDINGS BY THIS SUNDAY.
THIS CONFORMS WITH THE TIMETABLE MCDONALD DISCUSSED WITH
DENMAN BEFORE THE LATTER'S DEPARTURE FOR CHINA.
2.  JAPAN AND THE EC ARE WORKING ON A "MEDIUM" AGREEMENT
FROM THE JAPANESE POINT OF VIEW THAT DOES NOT REPRESENT
A REACHING SOLUTION.  IT DOES APPEAR TO BE A BIT BETTER
THAN THE EC FALLBACK POSITION DESCRIBED IN BRUSSELS LAST
WEEK TO MCDONALD AS A "CRUMBS-FOR-CRUMBS" ARRANGEMENT.
AT ANY RATE THIS CONFIRMS THE EC'S INTENTION NOT TO LET THE
JAPANESE BILATERAL HOLD UP THEIR TIMETABLE FOR A COUNCIL
REVIEW WHICH STILL IS SET TO BEGIN WITH A SPECIAL MEETING
OF THE COMMISSION ON MONDAY, FEBRUARY 26.  MCDONALD

title: The Ambassador in Argentina ( Stimson) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
Your September 28, 5 p.m. My September 25, 10 a.m., was telephoned tome at 8 a.m. by Havas Agency after all-night session House and was all they said. I now have official journal showing  attempt to delay vote by President's spokesman, Oyhanarte; but Radical members split, Lebreton voting with majority of 53, Saguier, probable next Minister for Foreign Affairs, voting with minority of 18, although a strong pro-Ally. Vote was worded, "The House declares that there should immediately be suspension of diplomatic relations between Argentine Government and Imperial German Government." It is now evident President will make no reply to Congress, as constitutional limit of session is to-night. Strike absorbs his attention.



Stimson

body:

PROPOSED SPECIAL ROMANIAN POLICY AT DECEMBER 5

GERMAN COMMENTS IN REF A BEFORE JANUARY 9, NEXT
DISCUSSION OF THIS ITEM.
RYAN

title: EXIMBANK VISIT TO CHINA
body:
1. FIRST SECRETARY OF CHINESE EMBASSY LI WEI CONVEYED
INVITATION TO EXIMBANK TO VISIT CHINA EARLY 1980 TO DISCUSS
TECHNICAL MATTERS RELATING TO EXIMBANK CREDITS.  BANK OF
CHINA PROBABLY WOULD BE HOST.  EXIMBANK GENERAL COUNSEL,
WARREN W. GLICK, AND VICE PRESIDENT, RAYMOND ALBRIGHT,
INDICATED EXIMBANK PREPARED TO SEND WORKING TEAM AS EARLY
AS FEBRUARY AND WOULD SEND WITHIN FEW WEEKS DRAFT OF AN
OPERATING AGREEMENT AND A STANDARD FORM OF LOAN AGREEMENT
FOR DISCUSSIONS DURING VISIT.  EXIMBANK BELIEVES VISIT
WOULD BE USEFUL ONLY WHEN CHINESE ARE READY FOR FULL
TECHNICAL DISCUSSIONS AFTER COMPLETE REVIEW OF DRAFT
DOCUMENTS.  THEREFORE, MORE SPECIFIC TIMING
WOULD DEPEND ON CHINESE READINESS FOR SUCH DISCUSSIONS.
2. AT REQUEST OF LI EXIMBANK FIRST WILL SEND LETTER CON-
FIRMING ACCEPTANCE OF INVITATION AND THEN WILL FOLLOW UP
WITH DRAFT DOCUMENTS.  COPIES WILL BE SENT TO EMBASSY. VANCE

Standley

title: 52. Editorial Note
body: In a memorandum to President Kennedy, April 1, 1961, McGeorge Bundy discussed "some of the key diplomatic issues in the probable diplomacy" regarding Laos, commenting that "the Soviet Union in agreeing to negotiation believes that it can secure eventually what it is taking rapidly by military action. Consequently, we should consider immediately what encouragement and hard assistance might be given to Thailand, Cambodia, and South Vietnam to strengthen their position with respect to a 'neutral' Laos which will provide a bridge to their borders for Communist subversion and guerrilla operations." title: The Chargé in the United Kingdom (Holmes) to the Department of State
body:
top secret 
6537. During general conversation on recent Commonwealth meetings Frank Corner Counselor New Zealand House stated subject of ANZUS raised in special meeting of UK, NZ, and Australia. At opening of meeting, Churchill vague and uncertain of topic under consideration. Later, consulting notes of previous meeting with Holland and Menzies, he worked himself up into considerable dither over noninclusion of UK. Corner would not comment on outcome and reticent re reactions of NZ and Australian Prime Ministers, but guessed Churchill would raise question with Eisenhower before fall meeting of council.
Corner commented that while he agreed there were "details" on which UK had reason to expect information, Churchill's position almost solely motivated by concern over political prestige. Specifically, Prime Minister dislikes idea of NZ and Australia moving closer to US unchaperoned by mother country.

title: Editorial Note
body: In a letter to Mr. Dulles dated December 27, 1951, titled "Memo for Ambassador Dulles", Prime Minister Yoshida discussed three topics. He urged Mr. Dulles to take part in the selection of an outstanding and well-known U.S. Ambassador to Japan. He stated that  the difference in policy between Great Britain and the United States on the China question posed a dilemma to Japan, urged that the two powers find a united clear-cut policy on the issue, and stated that once this was done Japan would go along, setting aside its own inclinations and interests for the sake of a common front of free nations. Lastly, the Prime Minister gave his views on what he described as the counter-infiltration of Communist China. (Lot 54 D 423)

title: No. 421.Mr. Bayard to Mr. Pendleton.
body:
[Telegram.]

Mr. Bayard informs Mr. Pendleton that from the reports of Mr. Sewall, United States consul-general at Apia, it appears that the state of affairs in Samoa is very distressing and that it can only be made worse by a continuance of the war. Mr. Sewall has been instructed to preserve a strict neutrality, but this Government is anxious in pursuance of its treaty with Samoa, to secure a peaceful adjustment of the difficulties and a considerate treatment of Samoans.
Mr. Pendleton is requested to suggest to the German Government the advisability of the immediate election of a king and vice-king, as agreed to in conference, and the issuance of identical instructions to the representatives of the treaty powers at Apia to favor such an election, leaving other matters discussed in conference for subsequent consideration.

June 8, 1970
Dear R.C.:
I was greatly relieved to hear the good
news about your successful surgery last Thursday.
Please make sure that you give yourself enough
leave for an adequate rest period and recuperation. I speak for both officers and staff of
the World Bank Group when I send you our very
best wishes for a complete and speedy recovery.
At the same time, may I use this opportunity to express my warm gratitude for your
kind personal assistance in helping to organize
my visit to Korea and China. The trip was immensely interesting and very efficiently organized, and, at the same time, most enjoyable.
I greatly appreciate your part in making it so
successful.
Sincerely,
Robert S. McNamara

title: Mr. Seward to Mr. Geofroy
body:
Sir: I have the honor to acknowledge the receipt of your note of the 26th instant, relative to the alleged formation of a society at New Orleans, the object of which is to make enrolments and purchase of arms and ammunition destined for Mexico, and stating that already transmissions of arms and munitions have been directed towards the frontier of the Rio Grande.
I have the honor to inform you, in reply, that letters have been addressed by this department to the governor of Louisiana and to Major General Banks, requesting an inquiry into the matters thus reported, with a view to insure a strict observance of neutrality on the part of officers and citizens of the United States.
Accept, sir, a renewed assurance of my high consideration.

WILLIAM H. SEWARD.
Mr. L. de Geofroy, &c.

280. Strictly confidential for Bonsal from Butterworth. Merle Cochran who will return to Paris from Moscow July 1 will succeed Dubois. After he completes writing his inspection report in Paris he will proceed to Hague for few days consultation with Amb and you prior to returning here for about 1 week's consultation. This info is to be kept strictly to ourselves until decision made regarding release. Livengood and Dubois are being similarly informed.
I think it would be helpful if you acquainted Cochran with the ins and outs of the polit situation in Holland and go over with him your ideas as to detailed manner in which working paper would have to be modified to meet insurmountable Dutch objections. It seems to us that Cochran should have when he departs from Batavia detailed workable  proposals which in essentials this Govt could support as basis for agreed settlement. [Butterworth.]

body:
1828. British Embassy Belgrade recently requested British liaison officer with Fourth Yugo Army to report on Slovene claims to Austrian territory.
BLO has replied that no exact claims have been made but only following general statements:
All territory containing Slovene minority should be included in Slovenia. All Stajersko and Korosko are rightly Slovene. Northern boundaries of these areas are vague but certainly include Vijlach and Klagenfurt and all territory south of Sava, east to Dravograd and possibly Volkermarkt east of Dravograd; probably all territory north of Drava will be claimed including Leibnitz. Tarvisio in Italy will certainly be claimed.
Following Partisan troops are north of River Sava: Fourteenth Division consisting of 5 brigades each about 1000 strong.


Kirk

title: The Acting Secretary of State to the Ambassador in Japan (Morris)
body:
New York Times and other papers published on April 16 statements to the effect that General Graves, Commanding the American forces in Siberia, had reported that the reason he did not go to the assistance of the Japanese detachment which was almost annihilated in an engagement with Russians at Haborvosk [Khabarovsk], Siberia, February 25, was because the Japanese had shot down women and children.
On April 17 Acting Secretary of War Crowell issued an official denial of the report with reference to Japanese brutality towards women and children. It developed that the report may have arisen from the fact that some troops representing a Russian faction had been charged with brutality towards women. Reports to this effect have been received here but no such charges have been made against the Japanese. This was made emphatic by War Department and the Department.
Polk

PATING IN CANTON TRADE FAIR, AND SENDING OTHER ECONOMIC

title: POSSIBLE FUTURE GUARANTEES TO SINGAPORE ON BOAT
body:
1.  INS/CO IS UNABLE TO LIFT RESTRICTION IN POSSIBLE FUTURE
GUARANTEES TO GOS ON BOAT REFUGEES PICKED UP BY U.S. SHIPS
AND NOT ACCEPTED BY OTHER COUNTRIES THAT ALL NOT
INADMISSIBLE UNDER INA WOULD BE ADMITTED TO U.S.
2.  GOS SHOULD BE INFORMED THAT INADMISSIBILITY CLAUSE
RELATES TO PERSONS WHO ARE EXCLUDABLE FROM THE UNITED STATES
UNDER CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF SECTION 212(A) OF THE
IMMIGRATION AND NATIONALITY ACT PERTAINING TO PERSONS WHO
ARE CRIMINALS, IMMORAL, SUBVERSIVE OR HAVE ENGAGED IN
NARCOTIC TRAFFICING.  IT ALSO INCLUDES PERSONS WHO HAVE
ENGAGED IN PERSECUTION OF OTHERS BECAUSE OF RACE, RELIGION
OR POLITICAL OPINION.  GOS SHOULD ALSO BE REMINDED THAT NO
PERSONS PREVIOUSLY GRANTED TEMPORARY ASYLUM IN SINGAPORE
HAVE BEEN REFUSED ENTRY INTO THE UNITED STATES FOR ANY OF
THE ABOVE REASONS.   VANCE

REQUIREMENTS ON PERFORMANCE BONDS FOR FOREIGN COMPANIES MAKING
SALES TO LIBYAN FIRMS AND ORGANIZATIONS. SECTION ON PERFORMANCE
BONDS IN ENCLOSURE TO REFAIR (ITEM 3, PAGE 2) NOTES: "IT IS

UNDER WHICH CLAIMS CAN BE MADE AGAINST THE BOND". HOWEVER,
SOME AMERICAN COMPANIES CURRENTLY ENGAGED IN SALES CONTRACT
NEGOTIATIONS WITH LARG HAVE REPORTEDLY BEEN INFORMED THAT NO
CONDITIONS MAY BE ATTACHED TO CLAIMS AGAINST PERFORMANCE
BONDS WHICH COVER SALES TO LIBYAN STATE AGENCIES OR STATE
ENTERPRISES. THUS LIBYAN PARTY WOULD BE FREE TO MAKE UNRESTRI-
CTED CLAIMS AGAINST ANY SUCH BOND.
2. SINCE AT LEAST ONE COMPANY IS DELAYING SIGNING MAJOR CON-
TRACT WITH LARG AGENCY PENDING CLARIFICATION ON PERFORMANCE
BOND MATTER, EMBASSY'S COMMENTS BY PRIORITY CABLE WOULD BE

STATES THAT BROKE RELATIONS.WE RESPONDED THAT SEVERAL

HAD ALWAYS EXPRESSED HOPE THAT PRESSURES COULD BE
RESISTED. HOWEVER, WE UNDERSTOOD THAT SOMETIMES THIS
WAS EXTREMELY DIFFICULT.

INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT TO HOLD OUT.

title: SURINAM TO RECEIVE WILLS
body:
SURINAM MINISTRY FOR GENERAL AND FOREIGN AFFAIRS AND
GUYANESE EMBASSY HAVE BOTH CONFIRMED THE GUYANA'S FOREIGN
MINISTER WILLS WILL VISIT SURINAM FEBRUARY 7. TALKS,

OTHER OUTSTANDING ISSUES INVOLVING THE TWO COUNTRIES,
COULD NOT BE ARRANGED EARLIER BECAUSE OF SCHEDULING
CONFLICTS. ALTHOUGH SURINAM'S PRIME MINISTER ARRON IS
NOT LIKELY TO FEEL IN A POSITION TO REACH ANY MAJOR AGREE-
MENTS WITH WILLS (WITH SURINAM'S 200-MILE ZONE NOT YET
OFFICIALLY ON THE BOOKS), DISCUSSIONS COULD BE THE
FIRST STEP ON A LONG ROAD TO IMPROVED RELATIONS BETWEEN
SURINAM AND GUYANA.

title: GOI DISCLAIMS KNOWLEDGE OF OVERTURE TO LIBYA
body:
1. HIGH FONOFF SOURCE TELLS US THAT GOI HAS NO KNOWLEDGE OF
VISIT TO LIBYA BY "DEVELOPMENT OF IRISH RESOURCES ORGANIZATION,"
LEAD BY WALTER J. HEGARTY (REFTEL). SOURCE DESCRIBED HEGARTY AS A
"DECENT CHAP" AND SMALL-TIME ENTREPRENEUR, WHO HOPES TO MAKE HIS
FORTUNE BY OPENING UP A DEAL WITH LIBYA. SOURCE DID NOT
APPEAR TO HAVE ANY CONFIDENCE IN SUCCESS OF VENTURE. ON OTHER
HAND, HE DID NOT INDICATE THAT GOI DISAPPROVED IN ANY WAY OF
ATTEMPT TO GET LIBYAN CAPITAL FOR OIL EXPLORATION OFF IRISH
COASTS.
2. NEWSPAPERS HAVE HAD SIMILAR REACTION TO THIS VENTURE:
PUZZLEMENT, BUT NOT DISAPPROVAL.
3. SAME SOURCE QUOTED IN PARA 1 TOLD US, HOWEVER, THAT IRISH
CONTINUE VERY STRONGLY OPPOSED TO LIBYAN SUPPLY OF ARMS TO
PROVISIONAL IRA. SOURCE HAD EXPLAINED THIS FORCEFULLY TO LIBYAN
REPRESENTATIVE AT PRESIDENT CHILDER'S FUNERAL, WHO WAS VERY
BADLY INFORMED ON IRISH SITUATION.

body:
1.  THE PRC EMBASSY IN SANTIAGO HAS BEEN VERY LOW KEY IN ITS
FUNERAL OBSERVANCE. IT NOTIFIED SEVERAL EMBASSIES -
REPRESENTING COUNTRIES WITH WHOM THE PRC MAINTAINS DIPLO-

BOOK, AND IN VIEW OF THE PRC AMBASSADOR'S LACK OF INTEREST
IN CONTACT WITH THE EMBASSY TO DATE, WE HAVE NOT OFFERED
TO SIGN THE BOOK.

title: The Ambassador in France (Edge) to the Secretary of State
body:
450. Your 265, July 27, 6 p.m. In conversation with M. Herriot last evening, reported in another telegram, I informally brought up the subject of the Franco-Belgian agreement and its discrimination against the United States, specifically mentioning the copper matter. The Prime Minister has asked me for a memorandum outlining the situation, which is now being prepared.
Replying to the last paragraph of the Department's telegram under reference, it is my understanding that France does not accord nations other than Belgium this special 2 percent advantage covered by the Franco-Belgian treaty. I am further informed that Switzerland has already put retaliatory measures in effect.
Edge

ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT THE GOI REQUIRES. HE INDICATED

title: Mr. Muruaga to Mr. Gresham.
body:
Dear Mr. Gresham: Yesterday afternoon, as agreed upon, I cabled to the minister of foreign affairs, but owing to the difference of meridian, my cablegram could barely reach Madrid before 12 o'clock that night.
Perhaps it would be wiser to delay all Congressional agitation whichsavors to imposition until the council of ministers could devise a provisional plan to assimilate in a certain measure the trade of both our countries.
This can easily be reached by mutual concessions, but could hardly be enforced abruptly.
The ministers will scarcely have time to-day to act upon the question at issue, although I expect to receive shortly some reference to it.
Believe me sincerely yours,
E. de Muruaga.

title: Consul Canada to the Secretary of State.
body:
[Telegram.]

 
Spanish Consul informs me two Spaniards of high social standing ordered to leave country within five days without being informed  of cause, time expiring today. He has advised them not to leave and will request Constitutionalist government if they should be arrested to show cause according to law and energetically protest against such order of expulsion. He requests my assistance in securing legal treatment for his countrymen and, as I am convinced in the case of these two men, request authority from the Department to make strong representations against arbitrary expulsion of these two as well as all other foreigners in the future.


Canada.

CUMULATIVE EFFECT OF FAILURE TO ACT PROMPTLY AND
WITH CERTITUDE IN DECISIONS OF THIS SORT, FAR FROM
APPEASING SOVIETS OR EAST GERMANS WILL AMOST IN-
EVITABLY BE TO INCREASED PRESSURE TO CUT BACK ON
MANIFESTATIONS OF BERLIN-FRG TIS. ACCORDINGLY, WE
URGE THAT ADDITIONAL EFFORTS BE MADE TO BRING BRITISH
AROUND. KLEIN

title: RISE IN COST OF LIVING ACCELERATING IN JAMAICA
body:
1.  ACCORDING TO COST OF LIVING FIGURES PUBLISHED IN
THE JULY 1978 CONSUMER PRICE INDICES STATISTICAL BULLETIN,
THE "ALL ITEMS" INDEX FOR JAMAICA WAS 191.0 IN JULY 1978,
AN INCREASE OF 6.8 PER CENT OVER JUNE 1978.  IN COMPARISON,
THE "ALL ITEMS" INDEX FOR JAMAICA IN JULY 1977 WAS 131.1,
AN INCREASE OF ONLY 0.8 PER CENT OVER THE PREVIOUS MONTH.
THE MOVING 1978 ANNUAL AND QUARTERLY RATES OF INCREASE OF
THE INDEX ROSE TO 42.0 PER CENT AND 27.3 PER CENT RESPECTIVELY.
2.  OF THE EIGHT CATEGORIES LISTED IN THE CONSUMER PRICE
INDICES (SEE REF. A), THE FOLLOWING FIVE RECORDED SIGNIFICANT
PRICE INCREASES:
PER CENT

(B) FOOD AND DRINK                               8.3
(C) HOUSING                                      7.3

title: NEED FOR PASSPORTS IN CASHING TRAVELERS CHECKS REQUEST DEPARTMENT  DISSEMINATE FOLLOWING THROUGH APPROPRIATE CHANNELS.
body:
REQUEST DEPARTMENT DISSEMINATE FOLLOWING THROUGH
APPROPRIATE CHANNELS.
MEXICO DOES NOT REQUIRE PASSPORTS OF MOST U.S. CITIZENS
TEMPORARILY VISITING IN MEXICO.  MANY AMCITS, ESPECIALLY
THOSE TRAVELING ON SHORT NOTICE, THEREFORE ENTER MEXICO
WITHOUT PASSPORTS.  WHILE THIS NORMALLY CAUSES NO PROBLEMS
WITH MEXICAN IMMIGRATION AND OTHER AUTHORITIES, SUCH
TRAVELERS FREQUENTLY FIND IT DIFFICULT OR IMPOSSIBLE TO
CASH TRAVELERS CHECKS WITHOUT PASSPORTS, WHICH ARE FORM
OF IDENTIFICATION REQUIRED BY MOST MEXICAN BANKS AND
COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS.  AMCITS WITH TRAVELERS CHECKS
WHO ENTER MEXICO WITHOUT PASSPORTS SHOULD THEREFORE HAVE
WITH THEM AT LEAST SUCH PHOTOGRAPH-BEARING ID AS DRIVER'S
LICENSE.  NON-PHOTOGRAPH-BEARING DOCUMENTS SUCH AS BIRTH
CERTIFICATES, CREDIT CARDS, ETC., ARE USUALLY NOT RPT NOT
ACCEPTED FOR TRAVELER CHECK-CASHING PURPOSES.  (EVEN WITH
PROPER IDENTIFICATION IT IS VIRTUALLY IMPOSSIBLE FOR AN
AMERICAN VISITOR TO CASH A PERSONAL CHECK IN MEXICO).
LUCEY

72. Department's 102, September 18, 1943. No action has been taken with respect to extending the Proclaimed List to Ireland following Russell's discussions with the Minister because of the opinion of the Department that such extension should not be permitted to be  coupled too directly with the request for the expulsion of the Axis missions. The question has now, however, been raised again by MEW. MEW believes that it may be an appropriate time to take such action since public impression of Anglo-American unity would be strengthened if the lists in Eire were joint as in most other neutral countries.

Please cable whether you believe extension of the list in May supplement would be desirable and, if so, whether there are any names now on the Statutory List that should not be included in the Proclaimed List.


Hull.

body:
OF SETTING UP G-77 SECRETARIAT
REFERENCE:  A)  PARIS 15561;  B) USUN 2019
FURTHER TO REFTELS, THERE APPARENTLY ARE TWO ASPECTS TO THE
IDEA OF SETTING UP A G-77 SECRETARIAT.  FIRST IS A PROPOSAL
BY JAMAICA THAT A SMALL SECRETARIAT BE SET UP TO PROVIDE
PURELY ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT TO JAMAICA IN ITS FUNCTION
AS THIS YEAR'S G-77 CHAIRMAN.  SECOND IS THE IDEA OF
ESTABLISHING AN OECD-TYPE SECRETARIAT TO PROVIDE TECHNICAL,
SUBSTANTIVE AND ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT TO THE G-77 IN ITS
NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE DEVELOPED COUNTRIES.  EVIDENTLY, THE
NAM GROUP DISAGREES WITH THIS SECOND IDEA BECAUSE IT DOES
NOT WISH TO SEE ITS SPECIAL FOCUS LOST IN THE WORK OF THE
LARGER G-77.  NEITHER IDEA IS CLOSE TO APPROVAL, ACCORDING
TO LOCAL REPS OF G-77 MISSIONS, ALTHOUGH THE JAMAICAN
PROPOSAL HAS SOME PROSPECT OF PASSAGE. YOUNG

66. It is urgently necessary for Department to know exactly what, if anything, Argentina is doing at the present time. title: Mr. Harold H. Tittmann, Assistant to the Personal Representative of President Roosevelt to Pope Pius XII, to the Secretary of State
body:
47. My 9, January 10th. Vatican asks me urgently telegraph following note dated February 15th.
["] On February 14th German Ambassador gave to Abbot Primate of Benedictine Fathers following memorandum.
'German military information states that announcements regarding German defense equipment in Convent of Monte Cassino are false. It is stated absolutely  incorrect that cannons, mortars or machine guns are there. No large size (grossere) troop concentrations are assembled there, that is in neighborhood of Convent. Moreover everything possible was done to prevent Monte Cassino from becoming transit center (Durchgangsplatz)'
Today Ambassador gave Abbot Primate and Vatican Under Secretary of State another memorandum as follows.
'According to statement competent German quarters there are not Convent Monte Cassino and its immediate neighborhood either cannons, mortars or machine gun emplacements. Neither are there are [any] German troops there.'"


Tittmann

title: The Consul at Geneva (Gilbert) to the Secretary of State
body:
14. Consulate's number 8, 3 p.m., and number 10, January 11, 6 p.m.

 Manchurian Commission formally "constituted" today.
 Due to Lord Lytton's inability to be present earlier, first meeting of the Commission will take place in Geneva on January 21.
 Lytton is urging that the European members of the Commission sail from Europe before the end of January and it is believed that other members of the Commission share his views and that there will be no delay in the Commission's proceeding.
 While it is a matter for the Commissioners to determine at their forthcoming meeting, it is still believed that they will decide to travel via the United States.

Gilbert

title: The Secretary of State to the Ambassador in the United Kingdom (Winant)
body:
No. 3744 

Sir: The Department's telegram No. 1097 of February 12, 1944, promised to send forward by air mail a copy of our suggestions made to the British Embassy as possible agenda for the forthcoming conversations on aviation matters. A copy of these suggestions is attached hereto.

For your information, it is apparent that there is some difference of opinion between the Foreign Office and Lord Beaverbrook in respect of having the Canadian Government join in the conferences. Lord Beaverbrook seems to have expressed himself informally to the effect that he did not want the Canadians present. The Canadian Government appears to have the impression that the British Government is expecting them to take part. We have been proceeding on the assumption that the Canadians would be represented in these talks, and propose to continue on that course.
Very truly yours,
For the Secretary of State: 

A. A. Berle, Jr.

STOOD THAT THE SOVIETS WOULD BE MAKING SIMILAR
PRESENTATIONS IN WASHINGTON, LONDON AND ELSEWHERE.

WOULD PERHAPS APPLY EVEN MORE STRINGENT SAFEGUARDS TO
ITS EXPORTS OF NUCLEAR MATERIALS AND TECHNOLOGY, AND
I CONFIRMED THAT WE VIEWED THE GUIDELINES AS MINIMUM
STANDARDS.

PNE'S, AND URGED THAT MOROKHOV AND I COMPLETE OUR
NEGOTIATIONS QUICKLY.  I REPLIED THAT WE WERE HOPEFUL
THAT AN AGREEMENT COULD BE REACHED IN THE COMING ROUND,
MOVING ON FORM THE PROGRESS AND MUTUAL HARD WORK OF
THE PREVIOUS DISCUSSIONS.

title: 221. Editorial Note
body:
On September 19, President Eisenhower and British Foreign Secretary Lord Home referred briefly to developments in the Congo in the course of a wide-ranging conversation. The relevant paragraph in the memorandum of conversation by John S.D. Eisenhower, dated September 19, reads as follows: 
"Lord Home said the Soviets have lost much by their obvious efforts to disrupt matters in the Congo. The President expressed his wish that Lumumba would fall into a river full of crocodiles; Lord Home said regretfully that we have lost many of the techniques of old-fashioned diplomacy." (Eisenhower Library, Whitman File, DDE Diaries)

title: Sir F. Bruce to Mr. Seward
body:
Sir: With reference to my note of the 30th of December, 1865, and to your reply of the 16th of February of last year, on the expediency of arriving at a common understanding as to the expense of maintaining foreign lunatics in asylums, I am instructed by her Majesty's government to inform you that from the answers received it appears that a general agreement on the subject cannot be arrived at.
Under these circumstances they are of opinion that there is no other alternative than that of dealing with such cases as they arise.
I have the honor to be, with the highest consideration, sir, your most obedient, humble servant,

FREDERICK W. A. BRUCE.

The Hon. William H. Seward, &c., &c., &c.

title: 399. Memorandum From the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Brzezinski) to President Carter
body: The Brazilian Foreign Minister made an extremely strong statement about foreign interference with Brazil's sovereign right to make international agreements, like the one with the Federal Republic of Germany on nuclear reprocessing facilities. The U.S. Embassy thinks Brazil is very sensitive to your remarks on nuclear energy exports, but that the "extreme aggressiveness" of the Foreign Minister's statement is a tactical effort to ensure that after U.S.-German discussions, the German-Brazilian agreement will be as close to the original as possible. Since President Geisel has made remarks stressing the "safeguard" provisions of the agreement, there is reason to believe that the Brazilian Government is not wholly united on the issue, and that they may just be trying to adapt to your position. In fact, recent and very private probes by people in the State Department indicate some willingness by the Brazilians to negotiate directly with us.

title: Mr. Tsui to Mr. Blaine.
body:
Sir: On the 12th instant I had the honor, under the instructions of the Imperial Government at Peking, to submit to you its views respecting the legislation now pending in the Congress of the United States as to the coming of Chinese to the United States. Since the date of that note I have received a second cablegram from the Tsung-li Yamen, in which I am instructed by it to urge upon you the importance to both Governments of the preservation of our existing treaties, which the pending legislation threatens to destroy. I can only repeat my earnest desire that you will do whatever you can to prevent any violation of these treaties by the Congress of the United States.
Accept, sir, etc.,
Tsui Kwo Yin.

title: The Ambassador in France (Straus) to the Secretary of State
body:
No. 1767 

Sir: In confirmation of my telegram No. 305 of April 6, 4 p.m., 1935, I have the honor to report that on that date a Secretary of the Embassy personally delivered at the Ministry for Foreign Affairs a note stating that the Government of the United States does not feel that it could usefully negotiate on the proposals (as outlined in the French memorandum and appendix, copies of which were transmitted to the Department as enclosures to my despatch No. 1529 of January 16) regarding the contemplated modification of the present customs regime in Morocco and formally protesting against the institution of the proposed modifications.
A copy of the Embassy's note, which as nearly as possible adheres to the text of the Department's telegraphic instruction No. 92 of March 16, 3 p.m., is attached hereto.
Respectfully yours,
For the Ambassador: 

Theodore Marriner


Counselor of Embassy

title: The Minister in Sweden ( Morris) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
682. On the 23d instant Swedish Minister for Foreign Affairs delivered a public address in Stockholm in the course of which he said that the Swedish Government would not sever commercial relations with the Central powers as a condition to obtaining foodstuffs from America. He stated that the population of Sweden need not fear a famine during the coming year and that the Government therefore will not be compelled to accept an agreement which is unacceptable to the Swedish people. The Minister for Foreign Affairs added, however, that the Government will endeavor to come to an agreement with the United States. A copy of the address is being forwarded to the Department by mail.




Morris

title: The Chargé in China (MacMurray) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
The French, British, and Japanese Ministers, considering it imperative to transfer Czech forces from Vladivostok to assist Czechs  in western Siberia, are requesting Russian Legation to arrange with the Russian railway authorities at Harbin for the transportation of these troops by the Chinese Eastern Railway; and upon receiving the expected favorable reply they propose simply to inform the Chinese Government that these forces are to pass through Manchuria.
In the absence of instructions I have not felt warranted in associating myself with these demarches which contemplate the probability of conflict with Bolshevik forces near Chita and which might therefore be considered as an act of intervention. I beg to request instructions as to the attitude to be taken in regard to this and other movements of the Czech forces in Siberia.

MacMurray

title: 240. Memorandum From the Executive Secretary of the Department of State (Tarnoff) to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Brzezinski)
body:
Events in the western Sahara are moving rapidly following Mauritania's separate peace with the Polisario. The Polisario has mounted a major attack on a Moroccan position at the southern end of the Moroccan portion of the western Sahara. Morocco appears to be in the process of claiming the former Mauritanian portion of the western Sahara. While such a move might temporarily reduce pressure in Morocco to attack Polisario bases in Algeria, the situation is unsettled and fighting could escalate rapidly. We recommend that the President send a friendly message to King Hassan acknowledging the problems he is facing and reiterating our interest in a peaceful solution. A proposed message is attached.

Peter Tarnoff

title: MIG-17'S CRASH IN MOGADISCIO
body:
1. TWO MIG-17' S COLLIDED OVER MOGADISCIO ON JAN. 23 AT
APPROXIMATELY 11:35 LOCAL AND FELL ON THE CITY BELOW. ONE
AIRCRAFT CRASHED IN A RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL SECTION, WITH
SOME LOSS OF LIFE, WHILE THE SECOND FELL IN A FIELD NEAR THE
SOMALI MIL CAMP.
2. THE MIDAIR COLLISON TOOK PLACE DURING A SOMALI AIR FORCE
SHOW OF STRENGTH FOLLOWING THE EXECUTION THE SAME MORNING
OF TEN SOMALI SHEIKHS FOR ANTI-GOVERNMENT ACTIVITY. MILIARY
AIRCRAFT ACTIVITY IN THE SKIES OVER MOGADISCIO BEGAN IN THE EARLY
HOURS OF JAN. 23 AND CONTINUED ON THROUGH MID-DAY, WITH MIG-21
FIGHTERS TAKING PART AS WELL. LOCAL MOSLEMS INTERPRET ACCIDENT
AS ALLAH'S JUDGMENT UPON GSDR AND SOMALIA FOR SLAYING OF SHEIKHS.
3. RADIO MOGADISCIO REPORTED ON EVENING OF JAN. 23 THAT
CRASH IN RESIDENTIAL AREA RESULTED IN EIGHT DEAD AND 132
INJURED, 17 SERIOUSLY. TWO SOMALI PILOTS ALSO PERISHED.
KIRK

The Ambassador in Argentina (Armour) to the Secretary of State
body:
1369. For the Under Secretary. I should appreciate your giving your personal attention to matter dealt with my telegram 1367, June 18. Armour

title: POSSIBLE SC MEETING IN TOKYO
body:
1.  DEPT CONTINUES TO FAVOR TRYING TO DISSUADE JAPAN FROM
SEEKING SC MEETING IN TOKYO AND AGREES IT WOULD BE USEFUL
TO MAKE ANOTHER ATTEMPT DISSUADE JAPANESE FROM INVITATION.
HOWEVER, DEPT DOES NOT BELIEVE WE SHOULD PUBLICLY OPPOSE
JAPANESE INVITATION OR THREATEN TO DO SO, WITH LIKELY
RESULTANT STRAIN ON US-JAPANESE RELATIONS AND WITHOUT
MUCH CHANCE OF DEFEATING JAPANESE INVITATION, ONCE
LAUNCHED.
2.  DEPT THEREFORE INTENDS TO CALL IN JAPANESE AMBASSADOR
HERE AT HIGH LEVEL IN IO TO EMPHASIZE ON GROUNDS OF ITS
CONCERN FOR UN FUNCTIONING OR STANDING ITS OPPOSITION
TO SC MEETINGS OUTSIDE NEW YORK, BUT STOPPING SHORT OF
INDICATING WE WOULD OPPOSE OR FIGHT JAPANESE PROPOSAL
IF IT FINALLY MADE.   INGERSOLL

1.  BEFORE THE FOREIGN MINISTRY CALLED IN CONOFF TO RECEIVE DOCUMENTS
TAKEN FROM JOURNALISTS PAUL HOFMANN AND LESLIE COLLITT, DEPUTY
FOREIGN MINISTER VEJVODA HAD TOLD ME AT A RECEPTION THAT WE WOULD
BE GETTING THEM BACK AND TOOK CREDIT FOR ARRANGING THEIR RETURN.  I
SAW HIM AGAIN FEBRUARY 2 AT DEPARTURE CEREMONY FOR THE DUTCH
FOREIGN MINISTER AND TOLD HIM THAT I APPRECIATED HIS ASSISTANCE WITH
THE DOCUMENTS, BUT THAT WHAT WE GOT BACK WAS NOTHING OF SUBSTANCE
- HE MIGHT HAVE SAVED HIS ENERGY.  VEJVODA REPLIED THAT, AS HE
HAD SAID EARLIER, THAT HE DID NOT KNOW EXACTLY WHAT WAS BEING
RETURNED.  HE SAID HE WOULD REPORT TO HIS SUPERIORS, HOWEVER, THAT
I WAS UNHAPPY ABOUT THE FAILURE TO RETURN THE JOURNALISTS' NOTES.
2.  VIENNA AND USBER MAY WISH TO INFORM HOFMANN AND COLLITT

title: The Ambassador in the Soviet Union (Standley) to the Secretary of State
body:
My Dear Mr. Secretary: Inasmuch as I have made no reports to the State department, on the Stalin-Churchill-Harriman negotiations, and the further fact that Mr. Harriman has no doubt reported in full to the President, I am forwarding herewith my personal observations  in regard to the Conference for such use as you may deem appropriate. I am also enclosing some photographs which may be of interest in connection with Mr. Churchill's visit.
You will note that these observations are in a more or less fragmentary form and necessarily so for they were received at various times from Mr. Churchill himself and from Mr. Harriman and the British Ambassador. I feel that you will be interested in learning that according to the British Ambassador, the question of the Soviet post war frontiers was not mentioned at any time during the conferences.
With my kind personal regards.
Very sincerely,

W. H. Standley

title: CARIBBEAN GROUP CONFERENCE OF RECIPIENT COUNTRIES
body:
1.  LIMITED OFFICIAL USE - ENTIRE TEXT.
2.  MINISTER OF FINANCE BELL WILL REPRESENT JAMAICA AT
BARBADOS CONFERENCE.  THIS REFLECTS JAMAICA'S VIEW OF THE
IMPORTANCE OF THE CARIBBEAN GROUP, PARTLY BECAUSE JAMAICA
HAS BEEN ITS MAJOR BENEFICIARY, AND ALSO TO SIGNAL
JAMAICA'S CONTINUING INTEREST IN REGIONALISM.
3.  JAMAICA'S APPROACH TO THE JUNE MEETING COINCIDES
WITH US POSITION INCLUDING THE BUILDING BLOCK APPROACH
AND THE EXPLORATION OF SPECIFIC POOPRTUNITES, AS IN
EXPORT PROMOTION AND TOURISM.
4.  ALTHOUGH REGIONAL ECONOMIC COOPERATION HAS SLOWED
DOWN IN RECENT YEARS PARTLY BECAUSE OF FINANCIAL
PROBLEMS, JAMAICA LOOKS TO THE CG AS PROVIDING THE
CARROT AND WHEREWITHAL TO ADVANCE REGIONAL COOPERATION.
JAMAICA WOULD VERY MUCH LIKE TO SEE THE CG GO BEYOND
THE CARIBBEAN DEVELOPMENT FACILITY.
5.  THE FOREGOING BASED ON COMMENTS BY SENATOR RICHARD
FLETCHER WHO LEAD JAMAICA'S DELEGATION TO LAST YEAR'S
CG MEETING IN WASHINGTON.
LAWRENCE

title: U.S. PROPOSED DEVELOPMENT SECURITY FACILITY
body:

MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS (VURAL) OF US PROPOSAL REGARDING
EXPANDED COMPENSATORY FINANCING FACILITY UNDER IMF AS SET

THAT DEVELOPED COUNTRIES ARRIVE AT CONSENSUS ON ESCHEWING
RECOURSE TO THE FACILITY IN ORDER TO PERMIT INCREASED ACCESS
BY DEVELOPING COUNTRIES. HE HAD LEARNED OF THIS US INTENTION
DURING RECENT SPECIAL SESSION OF UNGA AND FROM TEXT OF
SEPTEMBER 12 STATEMENT BY US EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TO IMF

REGARDS THE US PROPOSAL FAVORABLY AND WILL BE HAPPY TO
JOIN IN A CONSENSUS AMONG OECD COUNTRIES THAT FUTURE
RECOURSE TO THE CFF WILL BE SOLELY BY DEVELOPING COUNTRIES
THAT MEET THE ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA.
MACOMBER

title: 446. Memorandum From the President’s Special Assistant for National Security Affairs (Bundy) to Secretary of State Rusk and Secretary of Defense McNamara
body:
During this climactic week of the Canadian election campaign it is likely that intensified efforts will be made to implicate the United States in one way or another, especially by accusing us of trying to influence  the outcome. The President wishes to avoid any appearance of interference, even by responding to what may appear to be untruthful, distorted, or unethical statements or actions.
Will you, therefore, please insure that no one in your Departments, in Washington or the field, says anything publicly about Canada until after the election without first clearing with the White House. This applies to all contacts with the press regardless of the degree of non-attribution.
McGeorge Bundy

title: The Ambassador in Nicaragua (Stewart) to the Secretary of State
body:
638. Referring to my telegram No. 637 dated October 31, 6 p.m. An aide to President Somoza informed me this morning that the President recognizes that his recognition of the new government in  El Salvador was premature and a mistake. He confirmed that the action was taken following the receipt of an urgent request from the Mcaraguan Minister in El Salvador. In part, however, it was due to the President's absence on Lake Nicaragua off Granada and to misunderstanding of messages transmitted to him by Dr. Arguello the Foreign Minister who is now blamed for the affair. The aide said that President Somoza would accept any suggestions we might make to him in the premises and if we so desired would find some way to negate the recognition.
Repeated to El Salvador.


Stewart

title: Memorandum by General Marshall to General Yu Ta-wei
body:
OSE 291 
Dear General Yu: I have just received information from General Clement and also from Executive Headquarters indicating that the proposed meeting scheduled between Nationalist and Communist military representatives in Shantung province has been postponed because of General Chen-I's presence with his troops on the Chiao-Tsi front. The continued aggressive action of the National forces along the Tsingtao-Tsinan railroad is dominating the situation in Shantung.
In elaboration of my discussion with you yesterday, I wish again to mention my concern over the probability that aggressive military action during the present period will lead to irredeemable chaos. My concern is centered around the Hopeh and North Kiangsu situation, as well as the situation in Shantung province.

title: The Secretary of State to the President
body:
secret
 
[Dear Mr. President:] Have had useful visit at Paris. Yesterday devoted wholly to talks with top French officials largely in relation to EDC. While political difficulties are great, Stassen and I feel that there is real determination on part of present government, particularly Mayer and Pleven, to push this to a successful conclusion. There is still a hard road ahead, but we feel that ultimate success is possible and even probable.
Your State of Union message was very well received and slight initial concern about Formosa was quickly dissipated, so that French press this morning takes sympathetic non-critical view.
Today we met at SHAPE with Ridgway, Gruenther and many of your former associates, and then with Ismay, NATO Council and OEEC and believe we contributed to their morale and to understanding of your administration's friendly policies.
[Best regards,



Foster

body:

HAD ASKED ABOUT POSSIBILITY OF OBTAINING POWER GENERATING
SHIP ON EMERGENCY BASIS. DUE TO RECENT HEAVY RAINS, HYDRO-
ELECTRIC SITUATION IMPROVED AND ARMY HAS WITHDRAWN REQUEST.

FORMATION RE AVAILABILITY WOULD SUFFICE. INFORMATION ON
AVAILABILITY UNDER MIMEX WOULD ALSO BE APPRECIATED.

title: 109. Backchannel Message From the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Kissinger) to the Head of the Delegation to the Paris Peace Talks on Vietnam (Lodge)
body:
The President has asked that I forward to you the following message:
"I am in full agreement with Ambassador Bunker's views on the private talks as outlined in Saigon 16292 and have noted that instructions from State on this subject are generally consistent with Bunker's views. Nevertheless, I am reinforcing these views through a separate back channel message to you. I believe that the U.S. has been as forthcoming as can be reasonably expected in the talks thus far and direct that in subsequent meetings, Habib confine himself to confronting the other side with a number of direct questions designed to elicit their views. Lacking responsiveness on the part of the other side, Habib should avoid any reiteration of our position, avoid protestations of our good will, and avoid the hint of any new concessions on our part lacking reciprocity.["]

title: JEWISH NEW YEAR IN MOSCOW
body:
1.  NEW YEAR SERVICES AT ARKHIPOV STREET SYNAGOGUE WERE HELD
WITH ONLY ONE MINOR INCIDENT.  POLICE WERE OUT IN FORCE, AND
AS USUAL ON HOLIDAYS DIRECTED TRAFFIC (TAXI TRAFFIC CLEARLY
ORGANIZED) UP ARKHIPOV STREET, MAKING IT DIFFICULT FOR JEWS
TO DANCE IN STREET.  PASSING CAR HIT A YOUNG GIRL WHO WAS
TAKEN TO HOSPITAL.  SITUATION THEN BECAME TENSE AND POLICE
CLOSED STREET TO TRAFFIC BRIEFLY.  THERE WERE NO MAJOR
INCIDENTS SATURDAY MORNING.
2.  FRIDAY EVENING ATTENDANCE WAS ABOUT ONE-THIRD OF 1974.
ATTENDANCE WAS SO TIGHT THAT DOORS REMAINED OPEN UNLIKE LAST
YEAR.  WOMEN'S GALLERY WAS ONLY QUARTER FILLED SINNE TICKETS
WERE DEMANDED AND FEW HAD THEM.  NO MEMBERS OF THE HUMAN
RIGHTS MOVEMENT WERE OBSERVED AT THE SYNAGOGUE UNLIKE
SITUATION IN 1974.
STOESSEL

50. Your 126, August 27, 9 p.m.

title: PEACEKEEPING PAINS: PRESS COMMENT
body:
1.  IN EDITORIAL HEADLINED "PEACEKEEPING PAINS",
OCT 3 HALIFAX CHRONICLE-HERALD TAKES POSITION
THAT, AFTER 14 YEARS ON THE JOB, TIME HAS COME
FOR CANADIAN PEACEKEEPING FORCES TO BE WITHDRAWN
FROM CYPRUS.  NOTING THAT CANADIAN CONTINGENT
IN THAT COUNTRY IS NOW DOWN TO ABOUT 400 OF ALL
RANKS, EDITORIAL POINTS OUT THAT FORCE OF THIS
SIZE CONSTITUTES LITTLE MORE THAN A TOKEN,
ALBEIT ONE THAT TURKEY, GREECE, AND THE UN
WOULD PREFER TO SEE CONTINUED.
2.  WITHDRAWAL OF ITS CONTINGENT IN CYPRUS WILL
CERTAINLY BE NECESSARY, EDITORIAL STATES, IF
CANADA DECIDES TO SEND PEACEKEEPING FORCES TO
NAMIBIA.  EDITORIAL COUNSELS CAUTION ON SUCH A
MOVE, HOWEVER, NOTING THAT CANADIAN FORCES ARE
ALREADY THIN-STRETCHED ON PEACEKEEPING MISSIONS
ELSEWHERE.  CONFIDENCE IS EXPRESSED THAT CANADIAN
EXTAFF MINISTER DON JAMIESON WILL IN ANY EVENT
SEND FORCES TO NAMIBIA ONLY IF ALL DISPUTING PARTIES
AGREE TO UN INTERVENTION.
MOORE

title: The Secretary of State to the Consul General at Algiers (Wiley)
body:
477. For Murphy: The Treasury has proposed to the Finance Ministers of the United Nations and associated American governments the sending of an expert to Washington to enter into informal and tentative explorations of possible plans for monetary stabilization in the post-war period.
You are requested to make this known to General Giraud and to General Catroux and to inquire whether they could agree on such an expert who might assist in such exploratory discussions on the technical level by giving a French reaction to the suggestions discussed. Both the Treasury and the Department would hope that they would speak with one voice, so that we are not in the position of having the appearance of two interests, instead of one.
Cooperation between the two groups would be welcomed as a sign of increasing progress towards unity.


Hull

title: CANADIAN PARTICIPATION IN NATO HEADS OF GOVERNMENT
body:
1. DEPARTMENT OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS HAS ANNOUNCED THAT
CANADA WILL BE REPRESENTED AT NATO HEADS OF GOVERNMENT
MEETING IN BRUSSELS, JUNE 26, BY THE HONORABLE SENATOR
PAUL MARTIN, LEADER OF THE GOVERNMENT IN THE SENATE.
2. ALTHOUGH HIS PRESENT POSITION IS LARGELY CEREMONIAL,
SENATOR MARTIN IS SECOND IN PRECEDENCE IN CABINET (AFTER
PRIME MINISTER TRUDEAU), AND IS ONE OF CANADA'S MOST
DISTINGUISHED ELDER STATESMEN. BORN 1903 IN OTTAWA,
EDUCATED IN LAW AT TORONTO, HARVARD, AND CAMBRIDGE
UNIVERSITIES. ELECTED TO COMMONS IN 1935, AND IN EACH
SUCCESSIVE ELECTION UNTIL HE WAS NAMED TO THE SENATE
IN 1968. HE WAS SECRETARY OF STATE FOR EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
1963-68, AND WAS ELECTED PRESIDENT OF THE NORTH
ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION IN 1965. HE IS WELL
KNOWN TO MANY SENIOR US OFFICIALS, A FAST FRIEND OF
THE U.S. AND A STRONG SUPPORTER OF THE ATLANTIC
ALLIANCE.
PORTER
