title: METAL WORKERS PROVOKE INCIDENT AT CICAP
body:
1. FOLLOWING 5:00PM RALLY IN FRONT OF OPORTO LABOR MINISTRY OFFICE,
TWO THOUSAND STRIKING METAL WORKERS MARCHED PAST CONSULATE TO
DEMONSTRATE IN FRONT OF CICAP QUARTERS STILL GUARDED FROM WITHIN
BY PM UNITS. WORKERS CHANTED SUV SLOGANS AND DEMANDED THAT CICAP
BE REOPENED. LOUDSPEAKERS FROM BUILDING FINALLY ANNOUNCED RALLY
WAS OVER AND TOLD FINAL GROUP OF MARCHERS TO LEAVE AREA IMMEDIATELY.
SOMEONE IN CROWD ANSWERED WITH MOLOTOV COCKTAIL WHICH FAILED TO
EXPLODE AND GUARDS RESPONDED WITH TWO SALVOS OF CONCUSSION GRENADES.
A NUMBER OF PEOPLE RECEIVED SUPERFICIAL WOUNDS FROM GLASS BLOWN
OUT OF MOST WINDOWS IN BUILDINGS FACING CICAP QUARTERS ACROSS
NARROW STREET.
2. AS OF 7:00 PM CICAP AREA IS CLEARED.
3. COMMENT: UNFORTUNATE USE OF CONCUSSION GRENADES WILL ONLY INFLAME
ALREADY TENSE SITUATION AND IS BOUND TO BE EXPLOITED BY
SUV, CICAP AND LEFTIST ELEMENTS.
PENNER

1144. Department officially advised that a band of Yaqui Indians on May 20 drove off a large number of horses and cattle from a ranch 20 miles north of Guaymas and that a few days thereafter another band attacked farms in vicinity Potam, Sonora, killing a number of Mexicans and driving off livestock. Bring foregoing seriously to attention Mexican Government.


Polk

title: Memorandum of Conversation, by the Secretary of State
body:
Participants:
Secretary of State Hull, The British Ambassador, Lord Halifax, and Mr. Harold Butler
The British Ambassador called at my request.
He was accompanied by Mr. Harold Butler, who desired to come in to pay his respects. There was the usual exchange of greetings and of welcome.
I handed to the Ambassador a memorandum regarding the Free French situation, a copy of which is attached hereto. He said that he would send it to Mr. Eden with the request that, if Great Britain agrees to the proposal, he could then take the matter up with General De Gaulle and make him familiar with it with a view to a complete agreement between the Governments of Great Britain and the United States and the French National Committee.

C[ordbll] H[ull]

title: Lord Lyons to Mr. Seward.
body:
Sir: The attention of her Majesty's government has been drawn to the motion which was made in Congress during the recent session, with a view to putting an end to the arrangement between Great Britain and the United States limiting the naval force to be maintained upon the American lakes.
This arrangement has worked satisfactorily for nearly half a century. It has preserved both nations from a vast amount of inconvenience and expense, and, which is of infinitely more importance, it has warded off occasions of disagreement and quarrel. Her Majesty's government would view the abrogation of it with great regret and no little alarm.
I have the honor to be, with the highest consideration, sir, your most obedient, humble servant,

LYONS.
Hon. William H. Seward,
&c., &c., &c.

My November 24. Supreme Court of Panama dismisses writ of habeas corpus, holding that the resolution of the Governor is based on a law the constitutionality or unconstitutionality of which the Court is powerless to determine. Wicker.

title: 51. Memorandum From Helmut Sonnenfeldt of the National Security Council Staff to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Kissinger)
body:
I notice that Gerard Smith and Ambassador Thompson proposed that Dobrynin be informed of the resumption of US-Chinese talks before it becomes public knowledge.

In the last Administration it was standard practice for the State Department to provide Dobrynin with detailed records of the Warsaw talks. This was done at the Thompson and Bohlen level. The idea was to calm possible Soviet suspicions. It was also assumed that the Russians probably had some knowledge of the content of the talks from  Polish monitoring operations and that, therefore, there was no harm in providing them with the full record.
I believe that as a matter of style, and consistent with our general approach to the Soviets and the Chinese Communists, this practice of the last Administration should not be resumed in this one. I assume that you will want to call this to the attention of the Secretary of State.

title: FPS AD-1 ALARM MONITOR FOR COM RESIDENCE

title: CURRENT FOREIGN RELATIONS
body:

FOREIGN RELATIONS AT OUR COUNTRY TEAM MEETING AND FOUND

DEALINGS WITH AMBASSADORS OF OTHER COUNTRIES TO THE UN
ORGANIZATIONS HERE IN GENEVA.

RATHER THAN GENERALLY.  IT IS HANDY, HOWEVER, TO HAVE SOME

AGREED IN PREVIOUS MEETINGS ON BASIC PRINCIPLES. THESE ARE
THE NORMALIZATION OF DIPLOMATIC AND TRADE RELATIONS, EXCHANGE
OF DIPLOMATIC MISSIONS "AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE," AND PEACE-
FUL CO-EXISTENCE.

TALKS DID NOT DWELL ON PAST HISTORY BUT RATHER ON PRESENT AND
FUTURE RELATIONS. NO AGREEMENT WAS REACHED ON THE QUESTION OF
CAMBODIAN REFUGEES IN THAILAND, AND IT IS NOT TO BE MENTIONED
IN THE COMMUNIQUE, BUT THE CAMBODIANS REPORTEDLY SAID THAT
THEIR COUNTRY IS WILLING TO RECEIVE THEM. DETAILS CONCERNING
TRADE ARE TO BE DECIDED BY WORKING GROUPS OF THE TWO.

DISCUSSIONS WITH RTG OFFICIALS EARLY NEXT WEEK.

title: Vice Consul Silliman to the Secretary of State.
body:
[Telegram.]

 
Replying to your July 25, 5 p.m. Governor Carranza, in reply to Department's suggestions, will issue today a statement which he considers will be calculated to allay anxiety and inspire public confidence in the City of Mexico and elsewhere. In regard to personal guaranties, all concerned should remember that the demand of the Constitutionalists is for unconditional surrender. This will be vigorously insisted upon. Those entitled to protection will not be molested; others will be dealt with as circumstances of each case demand. Property rights will be respected and the property and rights of foreigners will be accorded the most ample guaranties. It is possible that Spaniards may expect trouble, as elsewhere. Excess of any kind will not be permitted.


Silliman.

title: GUATEMALAN VICE PRESIDENT VISITS CAIRO
body:
1. CAIRO PRESS NOVEMBER 18 REPORTS THAT GUATEMALAN VICE
PRESIDENT MARIO SANDOVAL ALARCON MET PREVIOUS DAY DURING EVENING
WITH PRIMIN SALIM AND DEPPRIMIN/FONMIN FAHMY. AHRAM REPORTS THAT
SANDOVAL EXPLAINED TO THE EGYPTIANS GUATEMALAN POSITION ON
BELIZE QUESTION AND WILL MEET ON NOVEMBER 18 WITH PRESIDENT
SADAT, ON OCCASION OF GUATEMALAN DECISION TO ESTABLISH EMBASSY
IN CAIRO.
2. DEPUTY PRIMIN HAFEZ GHANEM TOLD AMBASSADOR NOVEMBER 18 THAT
SANDOVAL, DURING MEETING EARLIER IN DAY, HAD URGED EGYPTIAN
SUPPORT FOR GUATEMALAN POSITION ON BELIZE IN UN. GHANEM STATED
THAT EGYPTIANS HAD MADE NO COMMITMENTS ON ISSUE, HAD MERELY
PROMISED TO STUDY MATTER. IN PART, STUDY CONSISTS OF DETERMINATION
OF PAST GUATEMALAN VOTING RECORD DURING ME DEBATES IN UN.

title: CUBA/JAMAICA COMMISSION MEETS
body:
1.  GOJ AND CUBAN OFFICIALS WILL BEGIN A WEEK LONG
MEETING IN KINGSTON ON NOVEMBER 11 TO DISCUSS TRADE
AND TECHNICAL COOPERATION BETWEEN THE TWO COUNTRIES.
ACCORDING TO THE "DAILY NEWS", GOJ DELEGATION WILL BE
HEADED BY MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS DUDLEY THOMPSON,
BUT MINISTER OF HEALTH MCNEILL, MINISTER OF HOUSING
SPAULDING, MINISTER OF INDUSTRY, TOURISM AND FOREIGN
TRADE PATTERSON, AND GOJ AMBASSADOR TO CUBA BEN CLARE
WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE AT DIFFERENT SESSIONS.  THE CUBAN
DELEGATION WILL BE HEADED BY MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND
SOCIAL CONSTRUCTION LEVI FARAH.  TOPICS TO BE DISCUSSED
INCLUDE TRADE, AGRICULTURE, CONSTRUCTION, FISHING, TOURISM,
PUBLIC HEALTH, AND SHIPPING.
2.  COMMENT:  SINCE PM MANLEY'S VISIT TO CUBA IN JULY,
THERE HAS BEEN STEADILY GROWING CONTACT BETWEEN THE TWO
COUNTRIES IN A VARIETY OF FIELDS.  GOJ CONTINUES TO LOOK
FOR WAYS TO APPLY CUBAN EXPERTISE TO JAMAICAN PROBLEMS.
GERARD

title: (U) FUENTES MOHR KILLING
body:
1. (C) DURING MARCH 14 CALL ON MINISTER OF GOVERNMENT DONALDO
ALVAREZ RUIZ, POLITICAL OFFICER REMARKED UPON INTERNATIONAL
OUTCRY WHICH HAD GREETED ASSASSINATION OF SOCIALIST POLITICIAN
ALBERTO FUENTES MOHR AND THE SENSE IN THOSE CIRCLES THAT THE GOG
WAS NOT PURSUING ITS INVESTIGATION AS VIGOROUSLY AS IT MIGHT.
SEEMINGLY SENSITIVE TO GOG'S IMAGE PROBLEM ON THIS QUESTION,
ALVAREZ NEVETHELESS ADMITTED THAT WHILE INVESTIGATION CONTINUES,
VERY LITTLE PROGRESS HAD BEEN MADE.  HE ALLUDED TO VAST NUMBER
OF UNSOLVED COMMON AS WELL AS POLITICAL CRIMES WHICH SEEMED TO
BE BEYOND POLICE INVESTIGATIVE CAPABILITIES.
2. (C) ALVAREZ OFFERED SPECULATION THAT THE TWISTINGS AND TURNINGS
OF FUENTES MOHR'S POLITICAL CAREER (FROM PR TO ALLIANCE WITH THE
DCG TO SOCIALISM) HAD MADE HIM MANY ENEMIES.  HE ALSO COMMENTED
THAT, IN THE CURRENT CLIMATE, IT WAS FOOLHARDY OF FUENTES MOHR TO
HAVE GONE ABOUT IN SUCH UNPROTECTED FASHION. BENNETT

title: ROK AID TO VIETNAMESE
body:
1.  ROK PRESS MARCH 30 REPORTED THAT ROKG IS CONSIDERING
AID TO VIETNAMESE REFUGEES.  TONGYANG DISPATCH FROM
WASHINGTON SAID AID PUBLIC AFFAIRS OFFICER HAD ANNOUNCED
MARCH 28 THAT SOUTH KOREA AGREED TO SEND SHIPPING TO
VIET-NAM AS PART OF INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE TO VIETNAMESE
APPEAL FOR AID FOR REFUGEES.  ACCOMPANYING ARTICLE NOTED
THAT ACTING FONMIN LHO HAD CONFIRMED THAT ROKG IS SINDIDER-
ING PLANS TO AID REFUGEES BUT HAD SAID THAT NO OFFICIAL
DECISION HAD YET BEEN MADE.
2.  PRESS MARCH 31 REPORTED THAT ROKG HAS DECIDED TO GIVE
MEDICAL AID TO VIET-MAN AND THAT OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT
WOULD BE MADE SOON.  ACCORDING TO PRESS, MINISTRIES
CONCERNED ARE CURRENTLY WORKING ON QUESTIONS OF COMPOSITION
AND DELIVERY OF AID, WHICH WILL REPORTEDLY TOTAL $2 MILLION.
CITING MOFA SOURCES, PRESS SAID USG IN RUTURN WILL DISCLAIM
ABOUT $4 MILLION EXTENDED TO ROK IN LONG-TERM USAID LOAN.
ERICSON

title: JIDDA MIDDLE EAST CONSTRUCTION EXHIBITION AND CONFERENCE (MECE 80)
body:
1. NOT HAVING RECEIVED TWO CABLES REFERENCED IN JIDDA 1305
WE ARE UNFAMILIAR WITH MECE AND APPARENT ORGANIZING
FIRM, "FAIRS AND EXHIBITIONS/ MENTIONED PARA 9 REFTEL.
2. KUWAITI BUSINESSMEN LIKE TO COMBINE BUSINESS WITH PLEASURE,
HENCE FIND TRAVEL TO LONDON, LAS VEGAS OR EVEN BAHRAIN CON-
SIDERABLY MORE APPEALING THAN TO JIDDA. HOWEVER MANY KUWAITIS
HAVE EXTENSIVE BUSINESS DEALINGS IN SAUDI ARABIA AND COULD
COMBINE THIS TRAVEL WITH VISIT TO EXPO IN JIDDA. WE SHARE
EMBASSY JIDDA'S JUDGEMENT THAT CONSTRUCTION IS A DECLINING
NEW MARKET FOR U.S. FIRMS.
3. WHATEVER THE PRODUCT, WE CONTINUE TO BELIEVE U.S.
FIRMS WILL MUCH MORE EFFECTIVELY PROMOTE SALE OF THEIR
GOODS AND SERVICES IN KUWAIT BY VISITS TO THE OFFICES OF
KUWAIT'S MAJOR BUSINESSMEN THAN BY PARTICIPATION IN
EXHIBITIONS IN THE ARABIAN PENINSULA.
MAESTRONE

title: DEATH OF PRINCE WAN
body:
PLEASE PASS THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE FROM THE SECRETARY
TO FOREIGN MINISTER PHICHAI:
QUOTE:  THE UNITED STATES HAS LEARNED WITH DEEP SADNESS
AND REGRET OF THE DEATH OF PRINCE WAN WAITHAYAKON WORAWAN.
THROUGH CLOSE ASSOCIATION WITH HIM DURING HIS SERVICE
AS THAI AMBASSADOR TO THE UNITED STATES, PERMANENT
REPRESENTATIVE TO THE UNITED NATIONS, PRESIDENT OF THE
UN GENERAL ASSEMBLY AND AS MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS,
A GENERATION OF AMERICAN LEADERS CAME TO KNOW AND RESPECT
HIM AS A SINCERE FRIEND AND AS A STRONG ADVOCATE OF
COLLECTIVE SECURITY AND THE BUILDING OF EFFECTIVE INTER-
NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS TO SERVE MANKIND.  HE LED A VERY
FULL AND USEFUL LIFE, BOTH IN THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY
AND IN THAILAND, AND HIS PASSING IS DEEPLY FELT BY ALL
WHO KNEW HIM.  UNQUOTE.   KISSINGER

title: The Ambassador in Austria-Hungary ( Penfield) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
1680. At 12.30 p.m. to-day Minister for Foreign Affairs called at the Embassy to explain that according to a Reuter message diplomatic relations between Germany and the United States had been broken. He wished that following personal message from him might be sent to the United States Government: 
Austria-Hungary and her allies were forced to commence the indiscriminate submarine warfare because the Entente declined the negotiations for peace on the basis proposed by Mr. Wilson, the basis that there were to be no victors and no vanquished. Austria-Hungary did not cease to point out to Mr. Wilson that she would be always ready to commence negotiations for peace on the basis above mentioned if the guarantees for it would be given. Following Mr. Penfield's wish the Minister for Foreign Affairs expresses the hope that the good relations between the United States and Austria-Hungary may be maintained.




Penfield

title: 327. Memorandum From President Kennedy to Secretary of Defense McNamara
body:
Are we keeping our Cuban contingency invasion plans up to date? I notice that there have been a number of new judgments on the amount of equipment that the Cubans have. I thought last October the number of troops we planned to have available was rather limited and the success of the operation was dependent upon, in large measure, our two airborne divisions getting in and controlling the two airfields. It seems to me that we should strengthen our contingency plans on this operation.
John Kennedy

title: The Minister in Guatemala (Whitehouse) to the Secretary of State
body:
125. Rodriguez Beteta and Orellana's son came to see me last night and told me the General was ready to follow the plan outlined in my 121, December 23, 2 p.m., but wanted a little time ... I asked how much; and they replied three or four days, which seemed reasonable. They explained that the new Provisional President must be someone that guarantees them from molestation and asked if you would recognize him at once. I told them I thought so if he was a suitable person. Time, in my opinion, is of great importance to avoid further trouble, and the sooner we have a regularly elected President the better. There are a good many people who, for personal reasons, desire to gain time before the elections, and among them is Recinos, but the country as a whole will suffer.
Whitehouse

title: Mr. Monroe, Secretary of State, to the governor of Tennessee.
body:
Sir: Intelligence has been received that some of the citizens of your State are collecting in the county of Giles, with the intention to make an incursion into some of the provinces of Spain, to join the revolutionary party in a contest against the existing government. As the United States are at peace with Spain, and such a movement is prohibited by law under severe penalties, the President has instructed me to communicate to your excellency this intelligence, *with a request that you would investigate its truth, and, should it appear to be well founded, give it all discountenance in your power. It is presumed that when the parties concerned in this proceeding are apprised of the sense of their Government, and, more especially, of the legal prohibition and penalties attached to it, they will not hesitate to decline it. [5]

JAMES MONROE.

The Governor of Tennessee.

[Telegram.--Extract.--Paraphrase.]

 
The Minister of Finance has served written demand on the bankers to answer by June 15 whether or not they will advance 19,000,000 taels more during June; otherwise he will get the money elsewhere. Calhoun.

title: 222. Telegram From the Department of State to the Embassy in the Soviet Union
body:
1160. Eyes only for Kohler from Secretary. I am puzzled by the timing and motivation of Soviet action in convoy holdup on autobahn. Following possibilities occur to me: 
 That we are heading for a major crisis and that Soviet efforts in recent months were part of a huge deception effort.
 That there has been a split in the regime in Moscow.
 That Khrushchev, beset with other difficulties, has felt it necessary to demonstrate a forceful policy in a manner which he did not consider too dangerous, and
 That Soviet military in Germany are trying to precipitate difficulties for one reason or another, such as preventing possible cutback in Soviet military.

Suggest you be alert to report promptly any signs that may develop in Moscow which would throw light on this problem and let me have any thoughts you have on the subject.
Rusk

title: 411. Editorial Note
body:
Secretary of State Dean Rusk left for Geneva on July 20. The Secretary held a series of discussions, which were essentially courtesy calls, with the other Foreign Ministers, Indian Defense Minister Krishna Menon, and Souvanna Phouma and Foreign Minister Quinim Pholsena on July 22. Memoranda of the discussions are in Department of State, Central Files, 110.11-RU/7-2262; ibid., Secretary's Memoranda of Conversation: Lot 65 D 330; and ibid., Conference Files: Lot 65 D 533, CF 2134-2141.
On July 23, Secretary Rusk signed for the United States the Declaration on the Neutrality of Laos. Attached to the Declaration was a 20-article Protocol. The texts of the Declaration and Protocol are printed in American Foreign Policy: Current Documents, 1962, pages 1075-1083.

title: The Acting Secretary of State to Senator Eugene D. Millikin
body:
My Dear Senator Millikin: Reference is again made to your letter of April 20, 1948, requesting the State Department's comments on S. 2511, a bill "Repealing section 202 (e) of the Sugar Act of 1948."
In view of the fact that the intent of this section of the Act has been widely misunderstood and that circumstances under which the use of this section might be considered desirable now appear remote, the Department perceives no objection to its repeal.
The Department has been informed by the Bureau of the Budget that there is no objection to the submission of this report.
Sincerely yours,
For the Acting Secretary of State: 

Charles E. Bohlen


Counselor

title: TANGOV DEMARCHE TO EC-9 ON RHODESIA AND NAMIBIA
body:
1. EC-9, NORDIC, AND POSSIBLY OTHER AMBASSADORS WERE GIVEN
PRESENTATION AUGUST 9 AND 10 BY FOREIGN OFFICE PRINCIPAL
SECRETARY NYAKYI (FOREIGN MINISTER IS IN COLOMBO) ON RHODESIA
AND NAMIBIA.
2. ACCORDING TO THREE DIPLOMATIC COLLEAGUES WHO WERE PRESENT,
NYAKYI'S REMARKS WERE NOT WELL-FOCUSED AND LEFT THEM IN SOME
DOUBT ABOUT OBJECTIVE OF MEETING. HOWEVER, MAIN POINTS THAT
EMERGED SEEMED BE:
A. TANGOV SEES ANY COMPENSATION OR GUARANTEE ARRANGEMENTS
FOR WHITE RHODESIANS AS ACCEPTABLE ONLY INSOFAR AS THEY
ENCOURAGE DEPARTURE;
B. BRITISH ARE "CONFUSED" ON NAMIBIA, SEEMINGLY FAILING
TOUNDERSTAND THAT DIRECT SWAPO-SAG NEGOTIATIONS ARE THE
ESSENTIAL ELEMENT IN ANY NAMIBIAN SOLUTION. (IN RESPONSE TO
QUESTIONS, NYAKYI AVOIDED CHARACTERIZATION OF SWAPO AS "SOLE"
AFRICAN ELEMENT BUT INSISTED IT MUST BE "MAIN" OR "DOMINANT"
ONE.);
C. TANGOV DID NOT KNOW WHAT US AND UK WERE CURRENTLY
UP TO RE SOUTHERN AFRICA AND WAS SOMEWHAT WORRIED ABOUT THIS.
SPAIN

title: Editorial Note
body:
In a statement before the United Nations Security Council on August 18, Mr. Jessup noted "suggestions" that the truce in Palestine might not continue. He then stated: "I should like to state in the clearest possible terms the view of the United States on this question. It is the view of the United States that the truce can be terminated only by the Security Council which on 15 July ordered the parties to observe the truce. No one of the States concerned, no group of the States concerned, can terminate the truce."
Mr. Jessup also noted that the resolution of July 15 dealt with an immediate and unconditional cease-fire in Jerusalem and instructed the Mediator to bring about the demilitarization of Jerusalem. He concluded that "The parties are under an obligation to cooperate with Count Bernadotte to this end." (SC, 3rd yr., No. 106, pages 3, 4)

ACCORDINGLY EMBASSY MAY USE ITS DISCRETION IN DETERMINING
LEVEL AND METHOD OF MAKING OUR APPROACH.

title: 144. Telegram From the Embassy in Egypt to the Department of State
body:
1722. Reference Embassy telegram 1632. Egyptian technical mission to Khartoum returned February 28 after discussion Sudanese-Egyptian currency linkage and commercial matters in general. Mission was headed by Nabih Younis, Under Secretary, Ministry Finance. Younis informed Embassy officer no agreements reached with Sudanese except with regard to terms of reference concerning topics discussed. Younis stated Sudanese reaffirmed earlier request that Egyptian delegation [come] to Khartoum to initiate Nile waters talks. Egyptian Government currently studying this new request. Younis felt that Sudanese seemed uncertain their position regarding Nile waters subject. Younis also commented his opinion general political situation in Sudan highly explosive and that Azhari government could not continue in this situation.
Byroade

title: Department Memorandum.
body: The Japanese Ambassador called today and I brought to his attention the fact that the newspapers kept reporting larger demands than those enumerated in the memorandum handed by him to the Department a few days ago. He said he had noticed the newspaper statements and denied the truth of them. I asked him whether he thought it possible that any demands had been made not included in the memorandum which he gave us and he expressed himself as certain that the memorandum included everything. I asked him whether he had any idea as to the influences that were responsible for these exaggerations and he said he did not. I asked him whether it was possible that the German influences in China might be responsible and he said that while they might, they had no evidence upon which to make such a charge.

title: DAIMLER-BENZ INVESTS IN SAUDI ARABIA
body:
DAIMLER BENZ AG, STUTTGART AND ITS SAUDI ARABIAN
SALES REPRESENTATIVE, E.A. JULAFFI " BROS., HAVE
ESTABLISHED A JOINT-VENTURE IN JIDDA TO ASSEMBLE
TRUCKS AND BUSES. THE JOINT VENTURE, NAMED NATIONAL
AUTOMOBILE INDUSTRY CO., LTD., IS CAPITALIZED AT
DM 21.4 MILLION (30 MILL. SAUDI RIYALS) OF WHICH THE
SAUDI-ARABIAN PARTNER HOLDS  74 PER CENT,AND DAIMLER
BENZ THE BALANCE. THE NEW FIRM IS SCHEDULED TO
EMPLOY 450 WORKERS AND TO TURN OUT 5,000 TRUCKS AND
BUSES ANNUALLY, PRIMARILY FOR THE SAUDI-ARABIAN MARKET.
OPERATIONS WILL BEGIN SOMETIMES IN 1977. A VOCATIONAL
TRAINING CENTER FOR ABOUT 80 MECHANICS WILL BE ESTABLISHED.
DAIMLER BENZ SALES TO SAUDI ARABIA  HAVE  INCREASED
SHARPLY IN RECENT YEARS,  AND IN 1974 REACHED 1,080
PASSENGER CARS AND 4,000 TRUCKS . ONE FIFTH OF DAIMLER BENZ
EXPORTS OF TRUCKS AND BUSES NOW GO TO ARABIAN COUNTRIES.

title: The Chargé in Argentina (Cabot) to the Secretary of State
body:
2438. Police began moving into Buenos Aires University buildings this morning 6 a.m. and by 7:30 were in full possession. Between 1,500 and 2,000 students arrested including some 130 girls. Action accomplished without incidents although street riot last night between opposing student groups resulted in one death and in dispersing another demonstrating group police caused several injuries. Santa Fe and Cordoba Universities have adopted resolutions similar to that Buenos Aires (Emtel 2430, Octdber 4, 8 p.m.) and it is expected remaining universities will do likewise. No reports yet received but presumably police either have occupied or will soon occupy all remaining universities of country. Reportedly 15 persons injured in connection with occupation La Plata University yesterday.


Cabot

title: The Ambassador in Russia (Francis) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
260. Just visited by member of All-Russian Central Executive Committee ... accompanied by local Commissar for Finance for government of Vologda who presented pathetic written appeal for flour stating require minimum 20,000 tons within a month and equal amount monthly thereafter. Urged shipments now en route elsewhere be directed to Archangel as needs are critical. Czech interference with Siberian Railway deprives Moscow, Petrograd, Vologda and surrounding section of flour and famine imminent.
I earnestly recommend compliance with request as such aid would be incalculably effective in securing good will of Russian people and would surely minimize if not end all opposition to intervention if any exists.
These officials confidently assert will pay for such food in Russian flax, leather, and butter or if that is unsatisfactory will pay gold which compensation I can arrange, but if no compensation game is worth candle.

Francis

title: The Consul at Chefoo (Roberts) to the Secretary of State
body:
Reference is made to the Embassy's telegram of October 7, 6 p.m., repeating Tokyo's number 1577, October 7, 10 a.m. to Department concerning Japanese interference with American firms here.

 Measures were not protective in any way and can be considered only a use of duress to obtain information about assets of American concerns.
 Managers of American firms deny that there was any advance understanding and claim that their first knowledge of measures came when police under Japanese orders descended upon them and stopped all communications with outside.
 Guards have now been removed from offices but are still maintained over warehouses belonging to Standard-Vacuum Oil Company and Texas Company to prevent removal of oil stocks.
 American businessmen were detained incommunicado in their business premises several hours until the Japanese authorities finished.



Roberts

GREATER THAN OUR INTEREST IN MAINTAINING WHAT ACCESS WE HAVE
TO THE GUINEAN GOVT.
2. THEREFORE, REQUEST CONAKRY BE GRANTED AN EXEMPTION FROM THIS
REQUIREMENT.
HAVERKAMP

title: GOJ RESPONSE TO H.R. 6550
body:
1. FONOFF (YAMAZAKI, 1ST NORTH AMDIV DEPDIR) VOLUNTEERED TO
EMBOFF THAT PRELIMINARY FONOFF REACTION TO H.R. 6550 RE
MICRONESIAN CLAIM WAS EMPHATICALLY NEGATIVE. APART FROM
SUBSTANCE, BILL WAS ILL-TIMED FROM FONOFF POINT OF VIEW. IT
WAS SEEN AS LIKELY TO COMPLICATE EFFORTS UNDERWAY WITHIN
FONOFF TO DEVELOP CONSENSUS IN SUPPORT OF COMPREHENSIVE LONG-
TERM AID PACKAGE, STARTING WITH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ON FISHING
AND AGRICULTURE AND LEADING TO SPECIAL STATUS FOR MICRONESIAN
IMPORTS AND JAPAN-MICRONESIA TRANSPORTATION LINKS.
2. YAMAZAKI AND OTHER FONOFF REPRESENTATIVES CALLED PARTICULAR
ATTENTION TO EXPLICIT MENTION OF JAPAN IN LEGISLATION, WHICH
THEY FOUND OFFENSIVE. THEY REGARD ISSUE AS CLOSED, AND PREVIOUS
$5,000,000 EX GRATIA AWARD AS FINAL. ANTICIPATE OFFICIAL GOJ
RESPONSE WILL BE ALONG THESE LINES; YAMAZAKI STATED THAT
"THIS IS ONE I HOPE WE DO NOT HAVE TO NEGOTIATE."

title: 136. Message From King Paul to Secretary of State Dulles
body:
This is a private message for your personal information owing to my deep concern about the present situation.
My talks with the Government and leaders of the opposition have reinforced my conviction that your assistance in securing inscription of the Cyprus question at the United Nations would be the most effective means by which the United States can help to  stop an alarming trend towards neutralism in Greece. There is general bitterness towards NATO. The positive sign of friendship evidenced by your support at the United Nations would counteract this disturbing tendency at a time when the serious illness of the Prime Minister is also likely to cause a political crisis in the near future.
The feelings of indignation of the Greek people with respect to the Turkish atrocities and feeling of abandonment by our friends run far higher than you may realize.

title: The Ambassador in Germany (Gerard) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
2780. Von Jagow's statement to me at 1.30 to-day sent in my last cable in which he said that if the torpedoing of Arabic was as reported in English papers that it would be disavowed and reparation  made, was, I learn informally, made by direct direction of the Chancellor who has taken this stand on his own initiative. Both the Chancellor and Von Tirpitz are hurrying to see the Emperor who is in Silesia. I hope you understand in view of the political situation here and influence of Von Tirpitz what a bold step has been taken by the Chancellor and Foreign Office and that you will make their road to disavowal and reparation as easy as possible under the circumstances. If made too hard Von Tirpitz and the party of [frightfulness] might again get the upper hand.



Gerard

title: The Ambassador in Iran (Morris) to the Secretary of State
body:
830. Three days ago Soviet censor in Iran held up five clear telegrams from Iranian ForOf to Iranian Missions abroad setting forth Iranian side of oil concession dispute. At request of Soviet Ambassador who refuses to speak to Prime Minister, British Ambassador asked Saed to send future telegrams of this sort in code to which latter agreed.
Today Russian censor informed British censor he had definitely stopped two official Iranian code telegrams, one addressed to Washington. It is assumed these are code versions of clear telegrams held up November 5.
British Ambassador has so far been unsuccessful in attempts to get explanation of this Soviet action which violates Anglo-Soviet-Iranian censorship agreement providing that Iranian Government is free to send any type of message in code or clear without interference.
Sent to Department repeated to Moscow as No. 72.


Morris

title: Memorandum of Telephone Conversation, by Mr. Gordon S. Reid of the Division of Central America and Panama Affairs
body: Mr. Rogers called me this morning to discuss the Nicaraguan situation and at the end of our talk stated that the Canadian Government understood that it was being invited to the Rio Conference in the role of observer. He then amended that so [and said?] that he understood the Brazilians were attempting to have Canada invite them. He said he thought I would be interested to know that the Canadian Government was hoping that they would not be invited either as an observer or in any other way. He ended by saying that it would certainly look funny to have the invitation issued to "the United Nations and Canada". When he finished the conversation he was still wondering whether that was an insult or compliment.

title: No. 339Editorial Note
body:
Secretary Dulles held a press conference on July 28. In response to a reporter's question about the growing strength of the Tudeh Party in Iran, the Secretary replied as follows: 
"Recent developments in Iran, especially the growing activity of the illegal Communist party, which appears to be tolerated by the Iranian Government have caused us concern. These developments make it more difficult for the United States to give assistance to Iran so long as its government tolerates this sort of activity."
The text of the Secretary's statement is printed in Department of State Bulletin, August 10, 1953, page 178.

title: The Secretary of State to the Chairman of the American Delegation (Davis)
body:
341. Your 657, May 24, 6 p.m. Please continue to exert all your influence against an adjournment of the Disarmament Conference until substantial conclusions have been reached. An adjournment by a fixed date irrespective of the state of the work would be an invitation to obstruction and dilatory tactics. We attach great importance to this point.
We shall consider the question of a possible reorganization of the Delegation if circumstances change or signature becomes more imminent. During this critical stage in the negotiations, however, we hesitate to alter in any way the present Delegation in Geneva which is functioning so effectively as a unit.


Hull

title: COFFEE: MONETARY BOARD RAISES MINIMUM COFFEE PRICE
body:
1.  ON APRIL 18, THE MONETARY BOARD RAISED THE "REINTEGRO
CAFETERO" (DOLLARS WHICH MUST BE SURRENDERED FOR PESOS --
MINIMUM COFFEE EXPORT PRICE) FROM US$188.40 TO US $202 PER
70 KILO SACK OF COFFEE.  THIS IS EQUIVALENT TO AN INCREASE
FROM US$1.22 A POUND TO US$1.31 A POUND.
2.  COMMENT:  SINCE THE FIRMING UP OF COFFEE PRICES, THIS IS
THE FIRST TIME THAT THE MONETARY BOARD HAS RAISED THE "REINTEGRO".
THE BOARD'S ACTION WAS PROBABLY PROMPTED BY THE FACT THAT AS THE
"REINTEGRO" PRICE WAS AROUND 18 CENTS A POUND BELOW THE WORLD
PRICE FOR COLOMBIA COFFEE, PRIVATE EXPORTERS HAVE BEEN MAKING
LARGER PROFITS ON RECENT COFFEE EXPORT SALES AT THE EXPENSE
OF THE NATIONAL TREASURY.  THE 12 PERCENT AD VALOREM TAX
ON COFFEE EXPORTS, WHICH EXPORTERS MUST PAY IS BASED ON THE
"REINTEGRO" PRICE.
ASENCIO

No. 4898

I can not fail to take this further opportunity of stressing the importance of closing this gap in the censorship of communications which, as may be seen from the enclosures, is necessary both from the negative and positive sides of censorship. Respectfully yours,

body: The First Committee of the General Assembly, basing its discussions on a Guatamalan draft proposal GA (II/SS), Annex, page 33, passed a resolution on May 4, by 33 votes to 7, with 13 abstentions. The subcommittee was to take into account "(a) Whether it is likely that such proposal  will commend itself to the Jewish and Arab communities of Palestine, (b) Whether it is possible to implement this proposal and make it workable, and (c) The approximate cost of such proposal." title: Extract from the Department of State Wireless Bulletin, February 27, 1950
body:
Israel has requested permission to buy arms and military equipment in the United States and the State Department is considering the request, according to Department officials.
Israeli Ambassador Eliahu Elath made the request last week, and presented a list of arms desired, State Department spokesmen told newsmen today.
News dispatches from London reported that Israel has made a similar request of Great Britain.
Officials in Washington pointed out that a relatively small amount of U.S. arms has gone to Israel in the past. Export permits are necessary for such shipments. U.S. policy generally permits shipments of arms if they are needed for the maintenance of order in the countries requesting them, the officials said.

title: BONGO UNHAPPINESS AT ABSENCE OF HASSAN FROM SUMMIT
body:
1.  SOURCE CLOSE TO BONGO HAS REPORTED TO US THAT PRESIDENT
IS EXTREMELY UNAHPPY AT FAILURE OF MOROCCAN KING HASSAN
TO ATTEND OAU SUMMIT.
2.  ACCORDING TO SOURCE, BONGO FELT HE HAD COMMITMENT FROM
HASSAN THAT LATTER WOULD COME PERSONALLY TO LIBREVILLE FOR
OAU SUMMIT.  ON BASIS OF THIS COMMITMENT, BONGO APPARENTLY
ASSURED OTHER CHIEFS OF STATE THAT HASSAN WOULD BE PRESENT.
THUS, BONGO IS NOT ONLY DISAPPOINTED AT HASSAN' FAILURE
TO APPEAR BUT ALSO FEELS THAT HE HAS BEEN MADE TO APPEAR
FOOLISH IN EYES OF SEVERAL OF HIS COUNTERPARTS.
3.  COMMENT:  WE SUSPECT BONGO WILL NOT LET PERSONAL PIQUE
AFFECT HIS PERFORMANCE ON EXTROARDINARY SUMMIT OR OTHER
ISSUES RELATING TO SAHARA.  HIS BASIC TIES TO MOROCCO
AND CLOSE FRIENDSHIP WITH MAURITANIAN PRESIDENT
OULD DADDAH SHOULD KEEP HIM FIRMLY IN THEIR CAMP
EVEN IF SOME OF PREVIOUS WARMTH DISSAPEARS TEMPORARILY
FROM BONGO- HASSAN FRIENDSHIP. STEIGMAN

title: EC PROPOSAL FOR REGISTRATION OF SEED MULTIPLICATION CONTRACTS IN THIRD  COUNTRIES
body:
THERE APPEARS TO BE SOME CONFUSION IN REF. A CONCERNING
EC'S PROPOSAL FOR REGISTRATION OF SEED MULTIPLICATION
CONTRACTS.  THE PROPOSALS, AS REPORTED REF. B, WOULD
REQUIRE COMPULSORY REGISTRATION OF SEED MULTIPLICATION
CONTRACTS IN THIRD COUNTRIES AND WOULD NOT REPEAT NOT
REQUIRE A NEW CERTIFICATION SYSTEM FOR THE SEEDS PRODUCED
UNDER SUCH CONTRACTS IN THIRD COUNTRIES.  A MULTIPLICATION
CONTRACT IS A FORM OF SUBCONTRACTING OF SEED PRODUCTION
WHEREBY SEEDS ARE FURNISHED TO A PRODUCER WHO REPRODUCES
THEM AND THEN DELIVERS THIS PRODUCTION TO THE COMPANY
ORIGINALLY SUPPLYING THE SEED.  THE U.S. CONCERN IS THAT
APPROVAL OF THE EC PROPOSAL TO REQUIRE REGISTRATION OF
SUCH CONTRACTS MADE WITH THIRD COUNTRY PRODUCERS WOULD
LEAD TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF ENFORCEMENT MECHANISMS THAT
IN TIMES OF OVERSUPPLY AND LOW PRICES COULD BE USED TO
RESTRAIN SUCH FOREIGN CONTRACTING AND THUS RESTRAIN TRADE.
HINTON

title: FUTURE OF NAVY MEDICAL RESEARCH FACILITY ON TAIWAN
body:
1.   WE NOTE IN THE JANUARY 23 ROC WEEKLY STATUS REPORT
THAT THE AGREEMENT TO EXTEND NAMRU-2 ON TAIWAN EXPIRES
THIS COMING OCTOBER.   WHILE WE, OF COURSE, DO NOT HAVE
DATA TO ASSESS FULL IMPLICATIONS, THIS WOULD SEEM TO
PROVIDE EXCELLENT OPPORTUNITY TO REMOVE THIS NON-ESSENTIAL
MILITARY UNIT FROM TAIWAN WITH MINIMAL DISRUPTION.
ELIMINATION OF THE UNIT WITH THE RESULTANT REDUCTION
(ALBEIT SMALL) OF MILITARY PERSONNEL ON TAIWAN WOULD
CONFORM TO OUR BASIC PLEDGE IN THE SHANGHAI COMMUNIQUE.
A NEW AGREEMENT BETWEEN US AND THE ROC COULD PROVIDE
ANOTHER EXCUSE FOR PEKING TO QUESTION WHETHER WE
ARE PURSUING THE PRINCIPLES OF THE COMMUNIQUE "IN
EARNEST."
2.   IF DEPARTMENT FEELS THAT TRANSFER FROM TAIWAN OR
TERMINATION OF NAMRU 2'S FUNCTION WOULD DEPRIVE USG OF
ESSENTIAL RESEARCH BENEFITS, CONSIDERATION MIGHT BE
GIVEN TO SHIFTING OPERATION TO A CIVILIAN AGENCY.
BUSH

No. 2.] 
Sir: I have the honor to inform the department that, immediately on the return of Mr. Hall, the minister of foreign affairs, from Jutland, and by his request, I met him on the 10th instant. His reception was frank and cordial, and while he alluded to the opinions held by my predecessor as different from mine, he expressed himself decidedly in favor of the administration and against the so-called confederates. I have the honor to remain your obedient servant,
BRADFORD R. WOOD.

title: Mr. Hay to Mr. Choate.
body:
[Telegram--Paraphrase.]

(Mr. Hay states that Peabody & Co. bring the Department's attention to newspaper reports to the effect that the British naval authorities have seized the steamer Sabine on the ground of carrying contraband cargo for the Boers; that they have shipments aggregating $30,000 to $40,000 made in January, to Mossel Bay, Algoa Say, and Durban, on orders from Cape merchants. The cargo is to be landed at British ports, the destination of the vessel being only such ports, and the port authorities may presumably, and are assumed to be bound to, prevent transshipment through British territory of contraband destined for the Boers. Mr. Hay deplores the action of the naval authorities, declaring that such seizure seems unnecessary and seriously destructive of legitimate American trade, and directs that Mr. Choate take necessary steps looking to the protection of the interests of American shippers.)

title: ILO: DUTCH CONSIDER POSSIBLE US WITHDRAWAL
body:
1. EMBASSY HAS LEARNED IN CONVERSATIONS WITH FOREIGN MINISTRY
AND SOCIAL AFFAIRS MINISTRY OFFICIALS THAT EEC MINISTERS
DISCUSSED IN THE JUNE 29-30 LONDON COUNCIL OF MINISTERS MEETING THE
DESIRABLITY OF URGING THE US TO REMAIN IN THE INTERNATIONAL
LABOR ORGANIZATION. ALTHOUGH THERE IS INTERNAL DISCUSSION
WITHIN THE DUTCH FOREIGN AFFAIRS COMMUNITY REGARDING DUTCH
TACTICS, THE OFFICIAL DUTCH POSITION REMAINS THE SAME AS
EXPRESSED BY FONMIN VAN DER STOEL TO AMBASSADOR IN REFTEL--
THAT THE DUTCH HOPE THE US WILL NOT WITHDRAW FROM THE ILO AT
THIS STAGE.

PRICE IN POLITICAL OBSTRUCTIONISM MUST BE PAID IN ORDER FOR THE
ILO TO CONTINUE TO EXIST--AN ORGANIZATION TO WHICH THEY SEE
NO SERIOUS ALTERNATIVE.
MCCLOSKEY

title: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt
body:
secret
 
Number 230. Former Naval Person to President most secret and personal. The only question which the Russians will ask or the only one that matters will be "Are you going to make a Second Front in 1943 and when and with what forces?" I cannot answer this except jointly with you because the forces we British can dispose of are obviously insufficient. Therefore, we cannot reply to Stalin's question until our Staffs have explored the possibilities together and hence my strong wish that your friends should come here. If this is not agreeable I am willing to come to you. We are all here sure that a talk whether at Moscow or Khartoum among the three Staffs apart from the heads of governments would not be useful.


Prime

title: Memorandum of Conversation, by Sheldon B. Vance of the Office of Western European Affairs
body:
confidential  Mr. Carlier stated that he wished to inform me that Ambassador Silvercruys had called on Assistant Secretary Key to say that the Belgian Government was disturbed by the tenor of statements made by the US Representative in the Trusteeship Council regarding the British and French Cameroons.
He added that he and Baron Dhanis had also called on Mr. Utter, in African Affairs regarding the same subject. He then told me what he had told Mr. Utter (for these remarks, see Mr. Utter's memorandum of conversation on this subject dated February 24, 1954).
Mr. Carlier emphasized that he had never in his experience received such an annoyed message as the one from the Belgian Foreign Minister on this matter.

title: Memorandum of Conversation, by the Secretary of State
body:
top secret
 
The primary subject of discussion was the topic raised in the proposed candor speech, the use of the atomic bomb and missiles.
In the main, Mr. Churchill and Mr. Eden expressed the view that our thinking on the subject was several years ahead of theirs, and that they were ahead of the rest of the world. They felt there was danger of our taking action which would be morally repellant to most of the world. It would be much better if there were an attack in any area which permitted of delay and possible localization if we did not instantly react with atomic weapons but waited for public opinion to develop, which it probably would do very quickly.




John Foster Dulles

title: NEXT FOREIGN MINISTER - ?
body:
1.  DURING MY MEETING WITH VP MUBARAK YESTERDAY, I
ASKED IF PRESIDENT SADAT HAS DONE ANY MORE THINKING
ABOUT A REPLACEMENT FOR MOHAMED IBRAHIM KAMEL.  MUBARAK
SAID THAT SADAT WOULD LIKE TO HAVE SAMIH ANWAR,
EGYPTIAN AMBASSADOR TO THE UK, BUT KNOWS ANWAR IS
NOT INTERESTED.  SADAT RECENTLY TOLD MUBARAK THAT
HASSAN KAMEL, DIRECTOR OF THE PRESIDENCY, HAD INDICATED
TO THE PRESIDENT THAT HE WOULD LIKE TO BE CONSIDERED
FOR THE POST.  MUBARAK SAID SADAT HAS NOT YET MADE UP
HIS MIND, BUT CLEAR IMPLICATION WAS THAT HASSAN KAMEL
IS A POSSIBILITY.  MUBARAK OBSERVED THAT THE PRESIDENT'S
PRESENT THINKING IS NOT TO APPOINT A NEW FOREIGN
MINISTER UNTIL AFTER THE SINAI TREATY TALKS ARE CON-
CLUDED.  EILTS

title: AID LEVELS FOR INDONESIA
body:
1.  SEVERAL CONVERSATIONS WE HAVE HAD HERE WITH
PRESIDENT SUHARTO, FOREIGN MINISTER, MINISTER
PLANNING AND OTHERS SUGGEST ONE OF INDONESIA'S
PRINCIPAL CONCERNS OVER REDUCTION OUR CONCESSIONAL
AID IS ITS EFFECT ON OTHER DONORS, PARTICULARLY
THIS YEAR.  SOURCE CLOSE TO PRESIDENT SUHARTO
REPRTED TO AMBASSADOR THAT PRESIDENT, AFTER HIS
MEETING WITH AMBASSADOR, REMARKED THAT, SINCE U.S.
COMMITTED TO ONE-THIRD OF IGGI TARGET, U.S. REDUCTION
WOULD MEAN, NOT JUST LOSS PORTION OF U.S. AID, BUT
POSSIBLE COMPARABLE REDUCTIONS IN AID FROM OTHERS.
2.  IN VIEW OF THIS, IF IT IS AT ALL POSSIBLE TO DO SO
FROM WASHINGTON STAND POINT, BELIVE IT WOULD BE
DESIRABLE, IN CONSULTATION WITH  OTHER DONORS, TO
SAY WE ARE EXPLORING POSSIBILITY OF APPLYING LESS
CONCESSIONAL AID TO OUR TARGET AND UNDERSTAND
INDONESIANS MAY BE PREPARED ACCEPT SUCH AID UNDER
IGGI IF IT IS CLEARLY DEVELOPMENT RELATED.
NEWSOM

I am, etc.,
Elihu Root.

title: Mr. Seward to Mr. Adams.
body:
No. 240.]

Sir: To-day the country is assuming that the fate of this unnatural war is determined by the great event of the capture of New Orleans, which was effected by a naval expedition on the 24th instant. I trust that the anticipation will be sustained.
Captain Bullock, of Georgia, is understood to have written that he has five steamers built, or bought, armed, and supplied with materiel of war in England, which are now about leaving or are on their way to aid the insurgents.
We are prepared to meet them. But the reflection occurs, are the maritime powers of Europe willing that the suppression of this insurrection shall be forever associated in the memory of mankind with the conviction that the sympathies of Europe were lent to the abortive revolution ?
I am, sir, your obedient servant,

WILLIAM H. SEWARD.
Charles Francis Adams, Esq., &c., &c., &c.

title: The Secretary of State to Special Representative Rodgers
body:
[Telegram]

 
293. Please communicate at once to General Carranza that the delay in appointing Commissioners for the Joint Commission is due to the fact that most of the men of the caliber and prominence which this Government desires in its Commissioners are so engaged as to prevent their acceptance of appointment; that the President prefers delay rather than to appoint men who are not of the highest standing in the United States; and that it is hoped the appointments will be announced within a few days. You may also express the hope that the Mexican Government will appreciate the wisdom of the President's course and will not misconstrue the delay which has taken place in the selection of the United States Commissioners.


Lansing

title: Municipal Council of Liverpool
body:
At a meeting of the mayor, aldermen and burgesses of the borough of Liver-pool, in common council assembled, held in the Town Hall within the said borough, on Wednesday, the 3d day of May, 1865--present, Edward Laurence, esq., mayor, &c., &c., &c.--it was

Unanimously resolved, That this council desires to record its horror and indignation at the atrocious murder of Abraham Lincoln, President of the United States, and to express its sympathy with the American nation under their severe loss, as well as to Mrs. Lincoln in the sad bereavement she has sustained.
And it was also

Resolved, That a minute of the foregoing resolution, under the common seal, should be sent to Mrs. Lincoln through the British minister at Washington.
[seal.] 

EDWARD LAURENCE, Mayor.
WILLIAM SHUTTLEWORTH, Town Clerk.

title: Minister Price to the Secretary of State.
body:
[Telegrams--Extracts.]

 
Referring to the Department's telegram of May 11, Panaman Minister for Foreign Affairs after a conference today states that the chief reason they have not signed the London Radio Convention  is that they feel that it would be {improper to become a signatory in view of their contemplating conceding to us the monopoly of wireless telegraphy in Panama. He states further it would be impossible to make response to my two notes within less than thirty days and that while they had nearly concluded to grant the monopoly of the wireless to us their action might have to be ratified by the National Assembly which does not meet until September. I asserted that this could not be under our treaty. He stated that Panama would not accept proposal (h) limiting the United States Government to erect only the four stations therein described.


Price.

title: Mr. Willis to Mr. Gresham.
body:
No. 33.] 
Sir: I have the honor to acknowledge the receipt of your telegram of January 12, 1894, sent to W. A. Cooper, U. S. dispatch agent at San Francisco, and by him forwarded, which reached here to-day.
Permit me to express my thanks for your words of approval.
I will, as directed, endeavor to keep the Department fully informed of the course of events and will, until further notice, consider that my  special instructions have been fully complied with, the Hawaiian question being, as you now inform me, submitted to the Congress.
I have further to acknowledge the receipt of your dispatch No. 6 of December 23, 1893, in regard to Department cipher, and your dispatch No. 7 of December 30, 1893, inclosing copies of documents in relation to Hawaiian affairs.
I am, etc.,
Albert S. Willis.

title: VICE PRESIDENT JUMBE TO VISIT CUBA
body:
1. TANGOV ANNOUNCED MAY 20 THAT VICE PRESIDENT JUMBE WILL
VISIT CUBA IN LATE 1978 OR EARLY 1979.
2. COMMENT. JUMBE SEEMS TO BE A SURROGATE FOR A RETURN VISIT
BY NYERERE IN RESPONSE TO CASTRO'S MARCH 1977 TRIP TO TANZANIA.
IT IS UNUSUAL FOR VISITS BY EITHER JUMBE OR NYERERE TO BE
ANNOUNCED SO FAR IN ADVANCE. END COMMENT.
3. FOR HAVANA: JUMBE'S TRAVELS HAVE INCREASINGLY TAKEN ON
CHARACTER OF STATE VISITS. HE IS ALSO NORMALLY TANZANIA'S
REPRESENTATIVE AT SUCH GATHERINGS AS OAU AND COMMONWEALTH SUMMITS.
THIS REFLECTS NYERERE'S INTEREST IN LIMITING HIS INTERNATIONAL
TRAVEL AS WELL AS PREPARATION FOR JUMBE'S APPARENT SUCCESSION
TO THE PRESIDENCY, POSSIBLY IN 1980. JUMBE'S TRAVELS HAVE BEEN
ALMOST ENTIRELY IN AFRICAN, ASIAN, MIDDLE EASTERN OR COMMUNIST
COUNTRIES. HE HAD HAD VERY LITTLE EXPOSURE TO THE WEST.
WALKER

title: NORWEGIANS SEND AMBASSADOR BACK TO MADRID
body:
1. NORWEGIAN GOVERNMENT DECIDED OCT 10 TO SEND ITS
AMBASSADOR THORE BOYE BACK TO MADRID. ACTION WAS
TAKEN AFTER CONSULTATION WITH NUMBER OF OTHER
COUNTRIES WHICH HAD RECENTLY RECALLED THEIR AMBASSADORS
TO SPAIN. BOYE WAS BROUGHT BACK TWO WEEKS AGO,
BEFORE EXECUTIONS IN SPAIN; HE WAS THE FIRST NOR-
WEGIAN AMBASSADOR TO BE RECALLED IN THIS MANNER
IN POST-WORLD WAR II PERIOD.
2. ACCORDING TO FOREIGN MINISTRY UNDER SECRETARY
ARNE ARNESEN, RECALL WAS DESIGNED TO UNDERSCORE THE
NORWEGIAN APPEAL TO SPAIN TO PARDON CONDEMNED
PRISONERS. BOYE WAS NOW RETURNING TO MADRID TO LOOK
AFTER NORWAY'S INTERESTS, AND TO INFORM GOVERNMENT
ABOUT DEVELOPMENTS, ARNESEN SAID, ADDING THAT THIS
REPRESENTED NO MILDER NORWEGIAN ATTITUDE TOWARD
THE EXECUTIONS. BOYE HAS TAKEN WITH HIM A MESSAGE
FROM THE NORWEGIAN TO SPAINISH GOVERNMENT.
BUCHANAN

title: 278. Telegram From the President’s Special Assistant for National Security Affairs (Bundy) to the Ambassador in Vietnam (Lodge)
body: CAP 63602. Deaths of Diem and Nhu, whatever their failings, has caused shock here and there is danger that standing and reputation of incoming government may be significantly damaged if conviction spreads of their assassination at direction of one or more senior members of incoming regime. Evidence available here is thin and conflicting, but simple assertion of suicide obviously will not end the matter. We believe that it is deeply in the interest of the regime to make prompt and full explanation, and if the deaths not by suicide, to emphasize with clear evidence all mitigating circumstances. They should not be left under illusion that political assassination is easily accepted here. Across the months of repression and increasing ineffectiveness, American people and government remember great services to freedom rendered by Diem over many years.

title: JOBERT STATEMENT ON FRENCH FOREIGN POLICY
body:
1.  ACCORDING TO AFP, IN COURSE OF RADIO INTERVIEW
APRIL 17 FRENCH FONMIN JOBERT SAID THAT HIS PROPOSAL FOR
A FEDERAL OR CONFEDERAL EUROPE IS A "LONG TERM THOUGHT",
BUT THAT IT ACCORDED WITH POMPIDOU'S IDEA.  JOBERT NOTED
THAT HE DIFFERED FROM FRG FONMIN SCHEEL, WHO SUPPORTS
THE PRINCIPLE OF MAJORITY VOTING WITHIN THE EUROPEAN
ORGANIZATIONS.  "REGARDING THE PLAN FOR THE CURRENT
CONSTRUCTION OF EUROPE," SAID JOBERT, "SCHEEL TAKES THE
VIEW OF INTEGRATION.  I TAKE ANOTHER VIEW.  THE STATES
DELEGATE CERTAIN POWERS TO A EUROPEAN GOVERNMENT, WHICH
IS AN EMANATION OF THE STATES."
2.  RESPONDING TO THE ACCUSATION THAT HIS POLICY HAS
ISOLATED FRANCE, JOBERT SAID, "AT THE UN, IN THE MAJOR
DEBATE ON RAW MATERIALS, FRANCE WAS NOT ISOLATED.  RE-
GARDING THE WESTERN COUNTRIES, THE FOREIGN MINISTERS OF
THE NINE WILL MEET SATURDAY AND SUNDAY IN BONN.  FRANCE
WILL BE THERE."
IRWIN

title: JAPANESE RED ARMY
body:
1.  DEPARTMENT CONCURS WITH JUDGMENT THAT LOD AIRPORT, JAL
HIJACKING, AND SINGAPORE FERRY INCIDENT WERE PFLP OPERA-

HELPED PLAN OPERATIONS OR IF JRA MEMBERS ACTED AS INDIVI-
DUALS.

THAT SUGGESTS THERE WAS COOPERATION BETWEEN JRA MEMBERS AND
PFLP IN RECENT HAGUE INCIDENT.  NATIONALITY OF TERRORISTS,
OBJECTIVE OF FREEING THEIR JAPANESE LEADER AND HIS ABORTED
PLANS TO FREE A JRA COLLEAGUE IN LIBYA ALL POINT TO AN
ENTIRELY JAPANESE AFFAIR.  AGAIN, NOT ENOUGH IS KNOWN ABOUT
THE JRA TO SAY WHETHER JRA ITSELF OR INDIVIDUALS PLANNED
THE HAGUE OPERATION.   KISSINGER

Department feels strongly that Shereefian Government should be included in invitations to adhere to treaty for following reasons: (1) Terms of treaty itself in article 3, paragraph 2; (2) the repeated statements which have roused expectation that treaty will be worldwide; (3) our own direct relations with Morocco, so that not to extend invitation would appear to single out Shereefian Government for discrimination. title: The Secretary of State to the Ambassador in Spain (Bowers)

40. Department's 25, April 20, noon. On July 27 the Department learned that the Department of Agriculture proposed to issue a new order modifying the April 19 order by limiting importation to the  period October 15 to March 15. At our request issuance of the order was delayed. The Spanish Ambassador was called in. He said the Spanish shipping season for grapes began the latter part of September and requested that the time be moved up to October 1. I took up the matter with the Acting Secretary of Agriculture who has agreed to modify the order. Under the modified order importations, always subject of course to the provisions of the April 19 order, may be made between October 1 and April 15. With the order thus modified the time limitation does not appear to affect adversely Spanish shipments.

body:
1484. Dept in suggesting changes in Emb text was governed by following two considerations: (1) to avoid insofar as possible contributing to deterioration morale and Nationalist position north China and (2) to avoid possibility of adding to hazards of those Americans who would decide remain even under imminent Communist occupation.
Telegraph final text as far in advance of release as possible.
Lovett

body:
No. 1] 
Sir: I have the honor to inform you that the King of the Netherlands received me to-day in private audience as minister resident at this court, in accordance with the established usages, when I presented my letter of credence, together with that of the recall of Mr. Pike. Immediately afterwards, by previous arrangement, I was presented in a special audience to the Queen.

I am, sir, very respectfully, your obedient servant,

HUGH EWING.

title: EX-VIETNAMESE NAVAL VESSELS AT SUBIC
body:
B. STATE 270178 (DTG 141657Z NOV 75)
1. IN MEETING TODAY WITH DEFENSE MINISTER PANGGABEAN,

THAT INDONESIANS HAD DECIDED AGAINST SHIPS AT SUBIC AFTER

BEEN WITHDRAWN. I AM CONFIDENT READY ACCEPTANCE OF
THIS BY PANGGABEAN AND COMPANY MEANS THAT DECISION TO
TURN DOWN SHIPS AT SUBIC HAS SUHARTO'S APPROVAL.

title: PRESS SPOKESMEN ON INDIA
body:
1.  FOLLOWING EXCHANGE TOOK PLACE AT JUNE 27 DEPARTMENTAL
NOON PRESS BRIEFING:
Q.  BOB, DO YOU HAVE ANY COMMENT TODAY ON THE ACTIONS TAKEN
BY THE INDIAN GOVERNMENT ON THE PRESS CENSORSHIP, AND IS
THE UNITED STATES MAKING ANY REPRESENTATIONS CONCERNING
THE PRESS CENSORSHIP?
A.  NO. ON THAT QUESTION, I WILL JUST MAKE ONE VERY BRIEF
COMMENT.  FIRST OF ALL, LET ME TAKE YOUR SECOND QUESTION
FIRST.
I AM UNAWARE AS OF THIS TIME OF ANY REPRESENTATIONS THAT
HAVE BEEN MADE.  I WILL BE GLAD TO LOOK INTO IT.
BUT WITH REGARD TO THE GENERAL QUESTION OF CENSORSHIP,
NATURALLY THE UNITED STATES HAS BEEN, AND CONTINUES TO BE,
OPPOSED TO CENSORSHIP OF THE PRESS OR ABRIDGEMENT OF THE
FREEDOM OF THE PRESS ANYWHERE.
2.  COMMENT BY WHITE HOUS: SPOKESMAN IS BEING TRANSMITTED
IN WIRELESS FILES.   INGERSOLL

title: NATIONAL COUNCIL OF CHURCHES TO JOIN CATHOLICS IN PROTESTS
body:
PROTESTS
1.  SECGEN NCCC-K, DR. KIM KWAN SUK, INFORMED EMBASSY THAT

SERVICES FOR THE RELEASE OF THE PRISONERS AND RESTORATION

AND THUS UNDECIDED WHETHER TO DEPART AT ALL FOR
SYNOD IN ROME.)
SNEIDER

title: SPECIAL BDG FLIGHT TO BANGKOK
body:
1. EMBASSY INFORMED BY RELIABLE AMERICAN AIRLINE SOURCE THAT
CIVILIAN AIRCRAFT MARKED BANGLADESH NUMBER S2-ABO LANDED
BANGKOK EARLY MORNING NOV. 4. AIRCRAFT IDENTIFIED AS CIVILIAN
VERSION OF C-8 BUFFALO, SIMILAR TO FOKKER F-27. THERE WAS NO
RPT NO PASSENGER MANIFEST AND PASSENGERS WENT QUICKLY THROUGH

PASSENGER LIST, BUT THIS WILL TAKE SOME TIME.
2. EMBASSY HAD NOT RPT NOT INFORMED THAI FOREIGN MINISTRY OF
FLIGHT, AS WE HAVE HAD CONSIDERABLE PROBLEMS WITH INDO-CHINESE
REFUGEES OVER PAST SEVERAL MONTHS AND DID NOT WISH TO GIVE
IMPRESSION WE WERE SOMEHOW INVOLVED IN ADDING TO REFUGEE FLOW,
BUT FROM DIFFERENT DIRECTION. BANGLADESH EMBASSY CLEARLY
UNWILLING TO GET INVOLVED IN FLIGHT IN ANY WAY. CHARGE
D'AFFAIRES, SALWDIN KAISAR, REPORTEDLY NOT AT EMBASSY,
AND SENIOR CLERK WHO ANSWERED PHONE CLAIMED IGNORANCE
OF WHOLE MATTER.  WHITEHOUSE  UNQUOTE  KISSINGER

title: PRIMIN ON MEAT QUOTAS
body:
1. I WAS SUMMONED TO THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE LAST NIGHT
AFTER MY RETURN TO CANBERRA FROM VICTORIA. THE PRIM WANTED
TO EMPHASIZE TO ME PERSONALLY HOW SERIOUS HE FELT THE SITUA-
TION TO BE WITH RESPECT TO MEAT QUOTAS. HE SAID IT WOULD BE
EXTREMELY DIFFICULT TO EXPLAIN TO THE AUSTRALIAN PUBLIC IF
THE QUOTA WAS CUT BELOW THE 632 MILLION POUNDS AND INDICATED
IT WOULD BE MUCH MORE DIFFICULT TO DEAL WITH POLITICAL
MATTERS HERE IF THAT WERE TO HAPPEN.
2. I POINTED OUT THAT THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF MEAT MOVING INTO
THE UNITED STATES (INCLUDING PUERTO RICO) AND CANADA HAS
BEEN GREATER THIS YEAR THAN PREVIOUSLY, BUT HE SAID THAT
TYPE OF ARGUMENT WOULD NOT WASH POLITICALLY. HE CONTINUES
TO BE VERY STRONG IN INSISTING UPON A FULL 632 MILLION
POUND QUOTA.
HARGROVE

title: The Chargé in Argentina (Cabot) to the Secretary of State
body:
secret 
232. I would greatly appreciate any information Dept can give me re its future plans for exposure of Nazi penetration in Argentina and Nazi links of Peron and clique. As I have previously pointed out Argentine people are becoming increasingly sensitive about direct attacks on Argentine Govt under present circumstances. Nevertheless, I must again emphatically register my belief that it is not fair to keep from Argentine people pertinent evidence in our possession re Nazi penetration. Delay in making facts known is bound to discourage democratic forces and lessen their chances of getting rid of totalitarianism in this country. I am particularly disturbed at possible repercussions of Acheson's statement yesterday since many authoritative indications both from Washington and this Embassy ever since Dept [apparent omission] have shown Argentine people that we have such evidence and have indicated that we intended eventually to publish it.
Cabot

body:
1.  ARRANGEMENTS FOR IOC MEETING HAVE BECOME SNARLED.
DURING CONVERSATIONS WITH JOHN SCOTT AND BOB LANKFORD,
WE LEARNED THAT OFFICIAL INVITATIONS TO MEETING HAVE NOT
BEEN SENT OUT BECAUSE GOTT DID NOT RECEIVE OFFICIAL
REQUEST FROM UNESCO HEADQUARTERS TO HOST MEETING UNTIL A
FEW DAYS AGO.  WHEN LETTER FINALLY CAME, IT INDICATED THAT
NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS AND SUPPORTING STAFF WAS LARGER THAN
GOTT HAD PROVISIONALLY EXPECTED.  IN THE INTERIM, GOTT WAS
BEING PRESSED BY HOTEL TO MAKE DEPOSIT ON ROOMS THEY HAD
BOOKED OR CANCEL, AND IN LIGHT OF UNCERTAINTY OVER WHETHER
GOTT WOULD HOST MEETING, ROOMS WERE CANCELLED.  AS A
RESULT, GOTT APPEARS TO BE RECONSIDERING WHETHER IN FACT
IT WISHES TO HOST MEETING AT ALL.  IF IT DOES, DATES
WILL PROBABLY BE MOVED TO MID-JANUARY, WHEN HOLIDAY RUSH
IS OVER.
2.  WE WILL REPORT ANY FURTHER DEVELOPMENTS ON THIS QUES-
TION AS THEY ARISE. FOX

INDIAN SUPPORT (RATHER THAN ABSTENTION) ON REVISED

title: The Minister in Egypt (Kirk) to the Secretary of State
body:
510. My 503, March 4, 10 [11] a.m. In conversation preceding delivery of communication Yemen representative outlined its contents and I was afforded opportunity for explaining situation along lines of Department's telegrams on subject. Most of his conversation, however, was devoted to professions of sympathy of Moslems with democratic cause and more particularly to expressions of friendship toward United States with which he said it was desire of Yemen to become more closely associated after war owing to reputed interest without ulterior motives of United States in small states.


Kirk

title: MESSAGE FOR EAGLEBURGER: VORONTSOV
body:

HAVE ALREADY DONE SO ON BASIS OF REFTELS, CALL HIM IN GAIN --

title: Mr. Campbell to Mr, Seward
body:
No. 18.] 
Sir: I have the honor to acknowledge the receipt of your despatches Nos. 17 and 18.
The continued sickness of my daughter, and other causes of a private and domestic nature, render it very important, in my judgment, that I should make a short visit to my home, and I will leave here this evening for that purpose.
Should the department have anything of importance to be communicated to me speedily before my return to this city, I respectfully ask that your despatches may be forwarded to me at Hamilton, Ohio.
I remain, sir, most respectfully, your obedient servant,

LEWIS D. CAMPBELL.

Hon. William H. Seward, Secretary of State, Washington,D. C.

title: BO PARLIAMENTARY ELECTIONS TO BE HELD
body:
1. ACTING PRESIDENT S.I. KOROMA ANNOUNCED SEPTEMBER 9 THAT
AUTHORITY TO HOLD THE TWICE POSTPONED PARLIAMENTARY ELECTIONS
IN BO DISTRICT HAD BEEN SIGNED BY PRESIDENT STEVENS PRIOR TO
STEVENS' PRIVATE VISIT TO EUROPE. KOROMA WARNED THAT "IT
WAS NOT UNLIKELY THAT PEOPLE WHO ENJOYED CAUSING TROUBLE
WOULD MAKE TROUBLE OUT OF THE EXERCISE" AND SAID "GOVERNMENT
WAS DETERMINED TO SEE THAT THE ELECTIONS WERE HELD IN A FREE
AND FRIENDLY ATMOSPHERE".
2. BEGIN LOU - DURING INTERVENING FOUR MONTHS SINCE LAST
POSTPONEMENT OF BO ELECTIONS (REFTEL) THE SITUATION IN BO
HAS EASED CONSIDERABLY. WITH NO OTHER DISTURBANCES TO COPE
WITH ELSEWHERE IN THE COUNTRY, GOVERNMENT HAS ADEQUATE
SECURITY CAPACITY TO INSURE BO ELECTIONS ARE NOT USED AS
SPRING BOARD FOR RENEWED EXTENSIVE VIOLENCE. END LOU.
LINEHAN

body:

VISIT IN WASHINGTON FOLLOWING NATO NUCLEAR PLANNING GROUP

title: DOGS LOCATE DRUGS AT AIRPORT
body:
1. ON MAY 12, THAI CUSTOMS AT DON MUANG AIRPORT SEIZED
APPROXIMATELY 23 KILOGRAMS OF MARIHUANA, PACKED IN TWO
SUITCASES. AFTER RECEIVING A TIP THAT A SHIPMENT OF

DETECTOR DOGS AT THE AIRPORT. THIS IS THE FIRST SUCCESS

TO MAKE GREATER USE OF THE DOGS AT THE AIRPORT.

title: The Ambassador in Russia ( Francis) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
2050. Judson saw Trotsky to-day with my approval as at yesterday's meeting of Allied chiefs I advocated unofficial effort to influence armistice terms at conference beginning to-morrow. No objection was offered to each chief's exerting such influence unofficially and not personally. Judson making full report to War Department. Says no friction attended first session and thinks some good accomplished. My desire was as indicated my 2039, November 28, 12 noon, to throw safeguards around separate armistice, if inevitable, that would protect other fronts and prevent transfer thereto of German troops now confronting Russian Army; also to prevent liberation of Austrian-German prisoners and Russian prisoners. Trotsky told Judson had thought of such provisos.
Allied chiefs still carefully avoiding recognition. Reports continue that Bolsheviki will not have majority in Assembly.



Francis

EB No. 826 8 October 1980

CONSERVATION MEASURES TO REDUCE
GASOLINE CONSUMPTION

1. This bulletin is part of a continuing program by the Inter-
agency Federal Energy Policy Committee to encourage energy conservation.
Maximum tire inflation is regarded as a highly cost effective method of
improving fuel economy. Tests have shown that properly inflated tires
can increase vehicle fuel efficiency by as much as 5 percent. A
small investment of time spent inflating tires to the maximum tire
pressure will provide dividends through increased miles per gallon.

2.  The Agency Motor Pool has adopted the policy of inflating
tires to their maximum pressure, and individuals are encouraged to

adopt a similar policy with assigned vehicles and their privately
owned vehicles.

TO FORD TRUCKS ONLY AND NOT TO OTHER BOYCOTTED TRUCKS,

REGULATION AGAINST FORD.

title: AUSTRALIAN VIEW OF ORDERLY DEPARTURES FROM VIETNAM
body:
1.  DEPARTMENT OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS (DFA) INFORMS US THAT FAMILY
REUNIFICATION PROGRAM FROM VIETNAM DIRECTLY TO AUSTRALIA IS
NOT WORKING.  ESSENTIALLY, GOA HAS NOT YET AGREED TO
PARTICIPATE IN AN ORDERLY DEPARTURE PROGRAM AND IS PRESENTLY
STYMIED IN FACILITATING FAMILY REUNION DUE TO LACK OF
AGREEMENT ON PROCEDURES WITH THE SRV.
2. GOA VIEWS ORDERLY DEPARTURE AS SEPARATE FROM FAMILY
REUNION, AND INVOLVING NORMAL IMMIGRATION CRITERIA.  AT THIS
STAGE THE GOA IS NOT PREPARED TO ACCEPT VIETNAMESE FROM SRV
WHO DO NOT FIT AUSTRALIA'S FAMILY REUNION CATEGORIES,
FOR FEAR OF REPERCUSSIONS FROM NUMEROUS ETHNIC GROUPS
ALREADY RESIDENT IN AUSTRALIA WHO OFTEN MUST WAIT YEARS
TO BRING IN OTHER THAN CLOSE FAMILY RELATIVES.
ALSTON

title: Memorandum by Mr. James C. H. Bonbright of the Division of Western European Affairs
body:
In the course of a telephone conversation with the Legation at Ottawa this morning Mr. Armour told Mr. Hickerson that he had recently seen both the Prime Minister and Dr. Skelton with regard to the liquor situation. Both were apparently very much upset to hear of Seagram's party for the "little Congress," referred to in Mr. Phillips' telegram to Mr. Armour.
From Mr. Armour's remarks it was obvious that what he had heard from Dr. Skelton on the subject was based entirely upon Mr. Wrong's pessimistic reports from here. The Canadians are apparently very much discouraged over the way the conversations between the distillers and our Treasury and Justice representatives are proceeding. So much so that Dr. Skelton even expressed the opinion that the Canadian Government might as well withdraw from the whole thing.

title: The Chargé in Mexico (Boal) to the Secretary of State
body:
219. Department's circular telegram August 9, 6 p.m. I have today communicated to General Hay the three points given in your telegram and made it clear to him that these were given to avoid any possible misconception arising out of press reports.
The General had no official comment to make but told me entirely personally that he could foresee that if West Coast nations of South America availed of the opportunity to secure American destroyers the Japanese and some European nations would sit up and take notice. He wondered whether it would serve as a precedent for the furnishing of European war vessels to the contending factions in Spain. If the opportunity were availed of by numerous Latin American Republics he foresaw the possibility of complications.
Boal

RECENTLY.  ONE IN PROTESTANT SUBURB NEWTONBREDA SHOT FOUR

ORIGINALLY APPEARED BE RANDOM SECTARIAN ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT

JAM BELFAST.  HOWEVER, VICTIM IS EX-BRITISH ARMY OFFICER AND
NOW CHIEF SECURITY ADVISOR TO HOUSING EXECUTIVE.  PROVISIONAL
IRA SUSPECTED OF ABOVE ATTACKS ALTHOUGH  IT HAS NOT YET CLAIMED
RESPONSIBILITY.  REASONS OBSCURE FOR ANOTHER INCIDENT MAY 11
IN WHICH CATHOLIC SOCIAL WORKER IN NORTH BELFAST WAS SHOT AND
WOUNDED.  VICTIM WAS ASSOCIATED WITH BRITISH YOUTH AND SOCIAL
WORKER NICK WHITE SHOT AND KILLED IN ARDOYNE MARCH.

title: No. 473.Mr. Frelinghuysen to Mr. Soteldo.
body:
Sir: I have the honor to invite your attention to the claim of Mr. John E. Wheelock, which has long been pending. In this connection I beg to refer to the conversation upon the subject had with General Guzman Blanco, when lately in this city, and to the Department's expectation that you were to be instructed to tender suitable reparation to Mr. Wheelock without prejudice to the real liability of Venezuela.
Permit me to ask, therefore, whether you are prepared to come to a definite understanding in regard to this matter, as the President greatly desires to dispose of it, if possible, before the reassembling of Congress in December next.
Awaiting your response, I avail, &c.,
FRED'K T. FRELINGHUYSEN.

Rockhill.

body:
144. My 143, June 15, midnight [noon]. In order to counteract the efforts of the Germans to keep the Bank of Brazil in a heavily overbought position in compensation marks and in its determination to reduce the trade in compensation marks, the Bank decided today to suspend the crossing of the compensation marks with the dollar or other foreign exchange. Until further notice the Bank will establish arbitrarily daily buying and selling rates for compensation marks. Today's selling rate of milreis 5.920 is higher than at any time since August 1935 when the compensation mark was first quoted separately on the exchange market. The Bank has widened the spread between the buying and selling rates to 320 reis compared to 200 reis previously.
Please inform Department of Commerce.
Caffery

body:
No. 9.] 
Sir: Mr. Appleton's despatch of May 22, (June 3,) No. 18, has been received.
It contains the orders in admiralty on the subject of the treatment of American vessels during the present condition of our internal affairs.
The subject seems to call for no special instruction to you, except to express to the Russian government the satisfaction which this government feels in regard to the conduct and friendly action of the Emperor.
Mr. Appleton is now with us, and we are deriving much profit from the information he gives. We learn your high appreciation of his conduct in his mission with pleasure.
I am, sir, respectfully, your obedient servant,
WILLIAM H. SEWARD.
Cassius M. Clay, Esq., &c., &c., &c.

APRIL 16-18, FOR WAYNE SMITH AND TOM KITSOS, TELEPHONE
NUMBER AT AMAT IS 31.68.50.
2. LOS CONTACT OFFICER WILL BE MR. ROBERT BLUMBERG, OFFICE
TELEPHONE 99.24.72, HOME 32.09.01

IN MISSION.
SORENSON

title: CLOVE SMUGGLING PLOT
body:
1. TANZANIAN PRESS JANUARY 14 REPORTS, IN STORY
DATELINED JAKARTA JANUARY 13, DISCOVERY OF 125 TONS
CLOVES BEING SMUGGLED FROM ZANZIBAR TO INDONESIA, UNDER
COVER STOLEN DOCUMENTS, IN CRATES PURPORTEDLY CONTAINING
PAPER FOR USIS. SEVERAL INDONESIAN BUSINESSMEN REPORTEDLY
BEING INTERROGATED IN CONNECTION WITH CRIME, AND SPOKES-
MAN FOR AMEMBASSY JAKARTA QUOTED AS SAYING USG SURPRISED
TO LEARN OF SMUGGLING ATTEMPT.
2. AS THIS STORY LIKELY GET INCREASED PLAY HERE, WITH
POSSIBLE ANTI-AMERICAN (WE INVOLVED  IN PLOT TO DEFRAUD
ZANZIBAR) OR CONCEIVABLY PRO-AMERICAN (USG FOILS SCHEME) OVERTONES,
WE AND AMCONSUL ZANZIBAR WOULD APPRECIATE DETAILS.
CARTER
